signals.topic: Structured Output schema generator ignores Java nullability markers, forcing all fields into required array and causing LLM output hallucination
signals.summary: When using `StructuredMessageCreateParams.outputConfig(Class)`, the internal schema generator treats all Java class/record fields as mandatory regardless of @Nullable annotations or Optional types, adding them all to the JSON Schema `required` array. This forces the LLM to hallucinate placeholder values ("null", empty string, dash) for genuinely optional fields, degrading structured output quality. Users attempted @jakarta.annotation.Nullable, @javax.annotation.Nullable, @JsonProperty(required=false), and java.util.Optional — all ignored.
aliases: Java reflection schema generator ignores nullable fields
structured output schema required array over-inclusion
nullable annotations ignored in JSON schema generation
signals.review_reason: Confirmed functional degradation: the schema generator incorrectly marks all Java fields as required regardless of nullability, which directly causes the LLM to produce hallucinated placeholder values in structured output. User impact is clearly demonstrated via code example and schema output. This is a workflow-runtime issue affecting the core structured output feature, not a cosmetic or edge-case problem. Keep=true with confidence=0.9 due to single-source constraint.

source_issues.title: [Java SDK] Structured Output: Java fields are always included in the required array, ignoring nullability markers
source_issues.evidence: User reports that all fields in a Java record are placed in the JSON Schema `required` array regardless of @Nullable annotation or Optional type. User shows caseNumber, parentCaseNumber, and ageAtIncident all marked required despite parentCaseNumber being annotated @Nullable. User reports LLM is forced to hallucinate 'null' strings, empty strings, or dashes to satisfy schema. User attempted @jakarta.annotation.Nullable, @javax.annotation.Nullable, @JsonProperty(required=false), and java.util.Optional — all ignored.

signals.topic: web_search_20250209 dynamic filtering causes excessive pause_turn — 50-60% request failure rate in production batch workflows
signals.summary: The web_search_20250209 tool's dynamic filtering (internal code_execution loop) hits a server-side iteration limit and returns pause_turn with ~110 content blocks but zero usable output on 50-60% of production requests. Failed attempts still incur full token costs. Setting allowed_callers: ["direct"] eliminates the issue (100% success rate, 46s vs 32min per request), but this parameter is undocumented and users are unclear on its stability.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: dynamic filtering loop causes 50-60%% request failures in batch processing. Each failed request incurs full token cost with no usable output, causing significant financial loss (~$0.15-0.25 per failure) and operational delays (9+ hours for 35 items vs 38 minutes with workaround). Critical production reliability issue.

source_issues.title: `web_search_20250209` dynamic filtering causes excessive `pause_turn` at ~110 content blocks — batch processing impractical
source_issues.evidence: 50-60%% pause_turn failure rate on production batch runs; ~$0.15-0.25 wasted per failed attempt; batch of 35 requests takes 9+ hours and completes only 50-60%% of items; connection drops during long streaming requests; workaround (allowed_callers: ['direct']) exists but is undocumented and stability unknown

signals.topic: Managed Agents session event streaming silently drops all events — streaming entirely broken
signals.summary: client.beta.sessions.events.stream() yields zero events because Stream.__stream__ is hardcoded to only match Messages API event names. All managed agents event types (session.status_*, agent.message, agent.tool_use, agent.tool_result, agent.thinking, etc.) are silently dropped. The bug was reproduced with a minimal test case (0 of 3 events received).
signals.review_reason: Core functionality completely broken: the managed agents event streaming pipeline is entirely non-functional. Every consumer of client.beta.sessions.events.stream() receives zero events. This is not a partial degradation — the entire streaming path is a no-op. It is a primary use case for the managed agents feature.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Managed Agents: client.beta.sessions.events.stream() silently drops all events
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro shows 0 of 3 events yielded; Stream.__stream__ if-chain has no fallback for unknown SSE event types; all managed agents event types silently dropped; events.list() polling still works — only streaming method is broken; entire managed agents streaming functionality unusable in SDK 0.93.0

signals.topic: Managed Agents MCP client only supports SSE transport — incompatible with Streamable HTTP-only servers (e.g. Apify)
signals.summary: Managed Agents MCP client (client.beta.agents / client.beta.sessions) only implements SSE transport. Apify deprecated its SSE endpoint on April 1, 2026 and now only serves Streamable HTTP, causing all Apify-based MCP server connections to fail at initialization with 'SSE data line is not valid JSON'. No client-side workaround exists.
signals.review_reason: Primary use case blocked: managed agents cannot connect to any Streamable HTTP-only MCP server. This is a breaking incompatibility with the current MCP spec that will affect growing numbers of MCP server operators as they migrate from SSE to Streamable HTTP. The failure is silent (no explicit error) and causes tools to be unavailable without user awareness.

source_issues.title: Managed Agents MCP client only supports SSE transport — incompatible with servers that have dropped SSE (e.g. Apify)
source_issues.evidence: Apify deprecated SSE endpoint April 1, 2026; MCP server 'apify' initialize fails with 'SSE data line is not valid JSON'; agent falls back to other tools and never uses Apify; no client-side workaround available; critical production blocker for users with Streamable HTTP-only MCP servers

signals.topic: pause_turn resumption with web_search: API rejects its own server_tool_use blocks — docs contradict actual behavior
signals.summary: When web_search returns pause_turn, the API's own documentation instructs users to resubmit the response as-is. But the API validator rejects the server_tool_use blocks it produced, returning a 400 error. The API is internally inconsistent — it generates blocks it then refuses to accept. Users must strip server_tool_use blocks and lose in-flight search state as a workaround.
signals.review_reason: API self-inconsistency: the API generates server_tool_use blocks it then rejects on resubmission. This is a clear API behavior bug that prevents users from following documented instructions. The workaround of stripping tool use blocks loses search state, degrading output quality.

source_issues.title: pause_turn with web_search: docs say re-submit response as-is, but API returns 400 — are we missing something?
source_issues.evidence: API returns 400: 'web_search tool use with id ... was found without a corresponding web_search_tool_result block'; the API's own documentation instructs users to pass the response back as-is; the API validator rejects the block it itself produced; workaround strips server_tool_use blocks, abandoning in-flight search state

signals.topic: pdfplumber broken in code_execution sandbox — charset_normalizer mypyc module missing
signals.summary: pdfplumber is documented as a pre-installed package in the code_execution sandbox but fails on import due to a missing mypyc-compiled C extension (charset_normalizer). Users relying on the agent to choose pdfplumber for PDF processing hit immediate ModuleNotFoundError. Only pypdf works as a workaround.
signals.review_reason: Key documented capability is non-functional: pdfplumber is listed as a pre-installed sandbox package but crashes on import. This blocks PDF processing workflows and forces users to manually override the agent's tool selection. While a workaround (pypdf) exists, it requires user intervention and defeats the purpose of agent tool autonomy.

source_issues.title: pdfplumber broken in code_execution sandbox — charset_normalizer mypyc module missing
source_issues.evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '81d243bd2c585b0f4821__mypyc'; pdfplumber is documented as pre-installed but unusable; fails immediately on import; workaround requires manually using pypdf instead; agent tool selection is compromised

signals.topic: Streaming responses have no idle timeout detection; ping and error events are absent from RawMessageStreamEvent type, preventing clients from detecting stalled streams
signals.summary: When streaming responses (messages.stream() or messages.create({stream:true})), if the server stops sending SSE events mid-stream due to network issues, server stalls, or connection problems, the client waits indefinitely. There is no idle timeout detection. Additionally, ping and error are not defined in RawMessageStreamEvent type, preventing clients from building their own watchdog. This causes real production hangs that completely block sessions with no automatic recovery.
signals.review_reason: count=3 (issues #867, #749, #998) + strong user impact evidence: a confirmed production incident (Claude Code session hung with 12,896 input tokens accumulated), multiple upstream Claude Code hangs referenced, and a documented SDK regression caused by reliability logic being in the wrong layer. This is a main-flow blocking issue — streaming sessions hang indefinitely with no automatic recovery, and users have no mechanism to detect or abort stalled streams. Meets P0 criteria: count>=3, main-flow blocking, sample links present. Note: #867 and #998 describe the same core problem from different angles; #749 adds the missing type definition that prevents clients from working around it.

source_issues.title: bug/proposal: infinitely hanging clients breaking bigger/complex sessions. Proposal: add Streaming Idle Timeout to Prevent Indefinite Hangs
source_issues.evidence: Real production incident: Claude Code CLI session hung indefinitely. Server stopped sending SSE events mid-stream, client waited forever. Session had 12,896 input tokens + 4,059 output tokens before hang. No timeout mechanism detected or handled the stall.

source_issues.title: include ping and error in RawMessageStreamEvent
source_issues.evidence: ping and error are valid SSE events from the server, but they are not defined in RawMessageStreamEvent type. This makes it impossible for clients to handle raw events properly or build custom idle detection on top of the SDK.

source_issues.title: Proposal: Ping-aware streaming watchdog (fixes #749, #867, and downstream Claude Code hangs)
source_issues.evidence: Proposal explicitly states the root cause: 'the client should adapt to the server and current load — not guess.' References upstream Claude Code hangs (#46987, #33949, #39755, #25979) and a v2.1.104 regression 'partial response received' caused by reliability logic duplication between SDK and Claude Code's closed-source cli.js.

signals.topic: toolRunner does not propagate container.id across iterations, forcing workaround that causes infinite duplicate tool-calling loop, completely blocking code execution use cases
signals.summary: Using client-side betaTools with code_execution_20260120 in a streaming toolRunner loop has two compounding bugs: (1) container.id from the previous iteration is not forwarded to the next request, causing a hard invalid_request_error; (2) using setMessagesParams as a workaround either errors immediately or causes the model to enter an infinite loop of duplicate tool calls with identical inputs. There is currently no working path for this use case.
aliases: setMessagesParams causes infinite tool call loop
signals.review_reason: The toolRunner container.id propagation failure + infinite loop workaround (count=1 for that specific bug) combined with the streaming indefinite hang (count=1, #867) form a cluster of related reliability failures that block the core streaming use case. Together these show systemic streaming reliability problems: both hangs/infinite loops and hard errors. However, #964 and #867 are distinct bugs (different root causes), so their counts don't merge under the same topic. #964 alone has count=1 but strong user impact evidence (no working path for a documented use case). #867 alone has count=1 but has a confirmed production incident. Combined review reasoning: both are P1 with clear blocking evidence, but neither meets count>=3 for P0 upgrade.

source_issues.title: Bug: toolRunner does not propagate container.id across iterations, and setMessagesParams causes duplicate tool call loops
source_issues.evidence: Bug 1: container.id is not included in the next request after runner.generateToolResponse(), causing invalid_request_error. Bug 2: setMessagesParams workaround causes infinite tool-calling loop — model repeatedly calls code_execution and calculate_sum with identical inputs. The two bugs compound: Bug 1 makes container.id forwarding mandatory, Bug 2 means no workaround exists. There is currently no working path to use client-side betaTools alongside code_execution_20260120.

source_issues.title: bug/proposal: infinitely hanging clients breaking bigger/complex sessions. Proposal: add Streaming Idle Timeout to Prevent Indefinite Hangs
source_issues.evidence: Real production incident documented: Claude Code CLI session (f35c7c15-802e-462b-b468-b000a96e40bb) hung indefinitely during a streaming response. Server stopped sending SSE events due to network/stall issues, client waited forever with no detection mechanism. 12,896 input tokens + 4,059 output tokens accumulated before hang. References related issues #842 and #844.

signals.topic: JSON.parse crashes with unhandled SyntaxError when model outputs regex-like escape sequences or Windows paths in streaming JSON
signals.summary: When Claude model emits strings containing escape sequences valid in other contexts but invalid in strict JSON (e.g., regex-like \d, \p, \s, Windows paths like C:\Users\), the streaming pipeline's JSON.parse throws an unhandled SyntaxError that crashes the entire Node.js process as an unhandled rejection. No recovery, no fallback — complete process termination.
signals.review_reason: This is a clear main-flow crash — the streaming pipeline throws an unhandled SyntaxError that terminates the entire Node.js process. Users have no recovery path; the application simply dies. Affects any user asking the model to produce JSON containing regex patterns, Windows paths, or LaTeX. Count=1 because only #996 directly describes this specific failure path (the partialParse issue is a separate root cause, covered by #986).

source_issues.title: bug(streaming): JSON.parse crashes on invalid escape sequences in model output
source_issues.evidence: The error is unhandled and crashes the Node.js process. The SDK should gracefully handle malformed JSON from the model, either by attempting lenient JSON parsing (JSON5 / repair strategies), returning the raw string with a warning, or emitting a recoverable error event instead of throwing.

signals.topic: partialParse in _vendor/partial-json-parser crashes on invalid JSON escape sequences from model tool call output
signals.summary: The partialParse function in the vendored partial-json-parser throws 'Bad escaped character in JSON' when the model emits tool call JSON containing characters like unescaped backslashes (e.g., PHP namespaces App\Http\Middleware). This kills the entire streaming response mid-stream, with no recovery.
signals.review_reason: Direct main-flow failure: the partialParse call during structured streaming throws without any try/catch protection, killing the entire stream mid-delivery. The crash occurs on a common real-world trigger (model output containing backslash-heavy strings like PHP namespaces). No workaround available. Count=1 because this is a distinct root cause from the standard JSON.parse crash in #996.

source_issues.title: partialParse in _vendor/partial-json-parser crashes on invalid JSON escape sequences from model output
source_issues.evidence: This crashes the MessageStream during input_json_delta accumulation, killing the entire streaming response. The root cause is in generate() which outputs string values verbatim without sanitizing invalid JSON escape sequences. Additionally, the partialParse() call in MessageStream is not wrapped in try/catch.

signals.topic: MessageStream accumulates streamed text using O(N²) string concatenation, causing severe performance degradation on long responses
signals.summary: MessageStream uses snapshot.content[i].text += delta.text in a loop, which is O(N²) in JavaScript due to string immutability. Each concatenation copies all existing characters. For 4K tokens, this is ~16x slower than optimal; for 10K tokens, ~100x slower. All users generating responses >2K tokens are affected with no workaround.
signals.review_reason: Significant performance degradation affecting all users generating longer responses, but it does not block the main flow — the operation completes, just slowly. Count=1 (single issue), no production incident evidence. Downgraded to P2 per rules (count<3, no P0-level user impact evidence like process crash or infinite block). The root cause and user impact are well-documented but the issue has not yet accumulated multiple independent reports.

source_issues.title: perf(MessageStream): O(N²) complexity in text accumulation during structured output streaming
source_issues.evidence: Throughput scales O(N²) rather than O(N). At 10K tokens, performance is ~100x slower than optimal. Workaround: none — the accumulation is internal to the SDK and cannot be avoided by users.

signals.topic: SDK crashes fatally on 429 rate limit, destroying multi-turn agent sessions with full progress loss and direct financial cost
signals.summary: When the API returns a 429 rate limit error during a multi-turn agent session, the SDK treats it as a fatal exception rather than backing off and retrying. This terminates the entire session, orphaning all accumulated progress. Three independent runs over 2 hours each crashed at the same point after completing 80-90% of work. Direct cost: ~$2.50 for failed runs that should have cost ~$0.50 in a single successful run. A workaround of adding sleep between turns and retry logic around query() does not work because the SDK raises the exception internally before the caller's exception handler can intercept it.
signals.review_reason: Direct financial loss ($2.50), full session destruction with zero progress recoverable, retry workaround demonstrably fails because exception is raised internally before caller exception handler fires. While count=1, the monetary loss, ironic fact that cheaper model is more reliable due to this bug, and deterministic crash pattern for any multi-turn agent hitting rate limits clearly meet P0 bar.

source_issues.title: Agent SDK should handle 429 rate limits gracefully instead of crashing
source_issues.evidence: 3 independent runs each destroyed after 80-90% completion; $2.50 direct cost; Retry-After header available but ignored; workaround fails because SDK raises exception before caller can intercept

signals.topic: query() string-prompt path closes stdin immediately, blocking MCP server initialization before any model invocation
signals.summary: When calling query() with a string prompt and mcp_servers configured, the SDK closes stdin synchronously immediately after writing the user message. The CLI then sends a control request to register the MCP server, but the SDK's transport.write() fails with 'ProcessTransport is not ready for writing' because stdin is already closed. This is a different code path from the stdin timeout issue fixed in PR #731 — the string-prompt branch in client.py unconditionally calls end_input() regardless of any timer. The failure is immediate (~2 seconds), deterministic, and blocks the entire use case of using custom MCP tools with the string-prompt API.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow (query() with mcp_servers) is blocked before any model invocation. Deterministic, reproducible, no partial success. Workaround exists but requires API shape change (ClaudeSDKClient instead of query()). Related to issues #295 and #730 (closed, same class of symptom, different code paths). Downgraded from P0 per rule: count=1 single repo, but P0 reserved for count>=3 or exceptional evidence.

source_issues.title: query() + mcp_servers: string-prompt branch closes stdin before MCP handshake, not fixed by #731
source_issues.evidence: Deterministic failure within ~2 seconds; blocks use case of MCP tools with query() string prompts; same root class as closed issues #295 and #730; workaround requires switching to ClaudeSDKClient streaming transport which changes the API shape

signals.topic: SubprocessCLITransport stderr anyio task group leaks cancel scope on every normal query() completion, causing 100% CPU loop
signals.summary: SubprocessCLITransport uses the same anyio TaskGroup + manual __aenter__/__aexit__ anti-pattern that was fixed in query.py by PR #746. On normal completion of async for message in query(...), asyncio's asyncgen finalizer runs close() from a different task context, causing a cross-task cancel_scope.cancel() + __aexit__(). Anyio cancel scopes have task affinity — exiting from the wrong task cancels the original consumer task and puts anyio's _deliver_cancellation in a 100% CPU spin loop. This fires on every single normal completion of the documented query() pattern. It accumulates one stuck scope per agent run until process restart.
aliases: anyio task group cross-task cancel scope
signals.review_reason: Process instability (100% CPU spin) on every normal completion of query(), accumulating until process restart. Same root cause class as previously-reported #454 and #776. High impact per occurrence but limited to 1 issue in dataset.

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leaks cancel scope on query() completion — same bug #454 / #776, fix #746 incomplete
source_issues.evidence: Same failure class as #454 and #776 (both closed); PR #746 fixed query.py but not subprocess_cli.py sibling; fires on every normal completion (documented usage pattern); deterministic 100% CPU spin; verified with 4+ consecutive completions showing clean pipeline after fix

signals.topic: Background task TaskNotificationMessage leaks into next turn's receive_response(), causing model to answer wrong question
signals.summary: When a background task (spawned via run_in_background=true) completes between turns, its TaskNotificationMessage is delivered in the next turn's receive_response() call. The model sees the stale notification in its conversation context and responds to it instead of the new user query. In multi-turn applications like chatbots, this causes the model to answer questions about stale background tasks rather than the current message. Workarounds like client.stop_task() are unreliable ('No task found' errors).
aliases: stale task notification in next turn
model answers wrong question after background task
signals.review_reason: User-visible wrong behavior: model answers wrong question in multi-turn apps. Clear message flow trace showing stale notification delivered before Turn 2 init message. Related to previously filed #558. No viable workaround.

source_issues.title: Background task notification leaks into next turn after receive_response()
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with test script; model responds to stale TaskNotificationMessage from Turn 1 when processing Turn 2 query; related to #558 (second query hangs after background task); stop_task() workaround fails with 'No task found' errors

signals.topic: ClaudeSDKClient cannot be used across different async task contexts, limiting use in complex async architectures
signals.summary: As of v0.0.20, a ClaudeSDKClient instance cannot be used across different async runtime contexts (different trio nurseries or asyncio task groups). The client internally maintains a persistent anyio task group for reading messages that remains active from connect() until disconnect(). All operations must complete within the same async context where the client was connected. This is a fundamental architectural limitation for complex async applications that need to pass clients across different task contexts.
aliases: cannot use client across task groups
signals.review_reason: Blocks use in complex async architectures (trio nurseries, multiple task groups). This is a core architectural limitation, not an edge case. Affects any user building non-trivial async applications with the SDK.

source_issues.title: Ability to Use ClaudeSDK Client from multiple async contexts
source_issues.evidence: Known limitation documented in client.py source; fundamental architectural constraint from internal anyio task group; no workaround available

signals.topic: PostToolUse callback hook return values silently discarded — data loss in live API calls and session transcripts
signals.summary: When PostToolUse hooks are registered as JavaScript callbacks only (no shell/prompt/agent/function hooks mixed in), the SDK takes a callback-only fast path in Xh that discards the hook's return value. updatedMCPToolOutput is never yielded to the live API call, and the session transcript JSONL keeps the original tool response instead of the replacement. Users must implement a workaround (TOON-encoding MCP tool results at transcript persist time) to compensate.
aliases: hook callback fast path drops updatedMCPToolOutput
MCP tool output override not persisted to transcript
signals.review_reason: This causes silent data loss: updatedMCPToolOutput is not propagated to the live API call AND the session transcript (which users rely on for replay/audit) retains the original unprocessed output. The workaround requires deep SDK internals knowledge. This is a production data integrity failure for any user relying on MCP tool output transformation hooks.

source_issues.title: PostToolUse callback hooks: return value (updatedMCPToolOutput) silently discarded, never persisted to transcript
source_issues.evidence: Hook return value is discarded in callback-only fast path; both live API call and transcript JSONL lose the replacement output. Root cause traced to Xh function branching logic in sdk.mjs.

signals.topic: outputFormat returns subtype 'success' with no structured_output for non-trivial schemas — core structured output feature fails in production
signals.summary: When using outputFormat with nested or complex JSON schemas, the SDK returns subtype 'success' but structured_output is undefined. The model produces correct JSON in result text, but the SDK fails to extract it. Users cannot use structured output for any real-world schema complexity, defeating the feature's purpose.
aliases: structured output broken for nested schemas
outputFormat loses parsed data on complex schemas
structured_output undefined despite valid model output
signals.review_reason: Structured output is a key differentiating feature for SDK users building type-safe applications. When it silently fails on any non-trivial schema (which is the majority of real-world use cases), users cannot trust the feature. The wrong subtype ('success' instead of 'error_max_structured_output_retries') also prevents proper error handling downstream.

source_issues.title: outputFormat returns subtype 'success' when structured_output is absent — should return error_max_structured_output_retries
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows simple 2-field schemas work but any nested schema (3+ levels, $ref, inlined arrays) fails with subtype='success' and structured_output=undefined. 4 comments indicate ongoing discussion and testing across multiple model versions.

signals.topic: Manual user pause (instance.interrupt()) is flaky — intermittent failure leaves sessions running indefinitely
signals.summary: instance.interrupt() does not reliably reach the expected completion path. In some cases, the 'interrupt() completed' log is never emitted, and the session does not pause. The failure is intermittent and tied to timing/state conditions that are not documented.
signals.review_reason: User pause is a critical control flow operation for production applications. Intermittent failure means sessions can run indefinitely without the ability to stop them — this is a production blocking issue. The unclear timing/state requirements also mean users cannot build reliable pause/resume workflows.

source_issues.title: manual user pause is flaky
source_issues.evidence: Failed log shows multiple interrupt() calls over ~4 minutes with no 'interrupt() completed' confirmation; success log shows immediate completion. Intermittent behavior confirmed by author with concrete session IDs.

signals.topic: SDK crashes with 'Claude Code process exited with code 1' in Docker container — blocks all containerized deployments
signals.summary: When running the SDK inside a Docker container, the Claude Code subprocess exits with code 1 immediately after initialization. The debug log shows startup proceeds through [init] configureGlobalAgents but the process then terminates. No error detail is surfaced beyond the exit code, making diagnosis impossible without SDK source access.
aliases: Claude Code subprocess exits code 1 in container environment
signals.review_reason: Docker container deployment is a standard production pattern. The SDK crashing immediately makes containerized deployments completely non-functional. The error is opaque (no meaningful message), leaving users without a path to resolution. Count=1 but severity is absolute (complete blocker for the affected environment).

source_issues.title: When calling the SDK in Docker, the following error occurs: 'Claude Code process exited with code 1'
source_issues.evidence: Full reproduction with debug log showing Claude Code 2.1.81 in Docker (Node.js v24.14.1, container root user) exits with code 1 after init sequence. Debug log shows initialization begins but process terminates without error detail.

signals.topic: Programmatic options.env is silently overridden by ~/.claude/settings.json — API key and endpoint control fails
signals.summary: options.env passed to query() does not override environment variables defined in ~/.claude/settings.json. The value from settings.json is used instead, contradicting documented behavior that 'programmatic options always override filesystem settings'. Also affects ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, preventing SDK apps from pointing to custom endpoints.
aliases: API key control via options.env broken
signals.review_reason: This breaks a fundamental expectation (programmatic config overrides filesystem config) that is explicitly documented. Developers who use Claude Code interactively and also build SDK applications cannot control which API key or endpoint the SDK uses. Multi-tenant applications and custom endpoint setups are completely blocked. The issue is externally documented as a known pitfall, indicating broad user impact.

source_issues.title: Programmatic options.env does not override env values in ~/.claude/settings.json
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly documented behavior violated. Workaround requires manually editing ~/.claude/settings.json, disrupting the developer's interactive Claude Code setup. Publicly documented as a known pitfall on external blog. settingSources: [] has no effect. Affects ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL control.

signals.topic: Claude runs successfully but does not post reply comments to GitHub Issues in issue_comment / labeled-issues workflows
signals.summary: Claude completes its task (visible in logs, exit code 0) but never posts the result as a comment on the GitHub Issue. This affects two distinct scenarios: (1) the general issue_comment workflow (agent mode, issue #891), and (2) the Bedrock + labeled-issues workflow (tag mode, issue #1216). Both have correct permissions set but no comment is posted.
aliases: Claude runs but no comment posted
signals.review_reason: Two independent issues (#1216, #891) describing the same symptom with different root contexts (Bedrock tag mode vs 1P agent mode). The core feature of posting Claude's result to the Issue is entirely broken in both scenarios, despite successful runs. This blocks the primary use case of 'Claude on Issue' workflows.

source_issues.title: Claude on Issue succeeds but does not post any reply comment to the GitHub Issue
source_issues.evidence: Workflow completes with Success, permission_denials_count is 0, but no comment is posted to the Issue. Main use case of 'Claude on Issue' is entirely blocked.

source_issues.title: Issue comment workflow: Claude runs but doesn't post comments to issues
source_issues.evidence: Claude runs, produces result, but result is not posted as a comment. Only appears in Actions run summary. Issue open since Feb 2026, still unresolved.

signals.topic: Git credentials are overwritten by the action, causing subsequent git push operations to fail
signals.summary: The action overwrites git credentials set by previous steps (e.g., GitHub App token from actions/create-github-app-token), causing later `git push` commands to fail with 'Authentication failed'. The action modifies global git config instead of isolating its own environment.
signals.review_reason: Main flow is fully blocked. The user cannot push commits after Claude makes them, which is a core use case of the action. Explicit step-by-step reproduction and clear user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: Git credentials are overwritten by this action
source_issues.evidence: Git push fails with 'Authentication failed' after the action step. Requires manual workaround of re-setting http.extraheader via git config. Main flow (commit + push) is blocked.

signals.topic: Action fails at GitHub App OIDC token exchange with HTTP 401 Unauthorized, preventing any workflow execution
signals.summary: On first-run setup, the action attempts OIDC token exchange for a GitHub App installation token and consistently fails with '401 Unauthorized - Failed to get GitHub App installation token', despite the user's configuration being correct. The action retries 3 times then exits with code 1 before Claude ever runs.
signals.review_reason: The action completely fails to start, exiting before Claude makes any API call. This is a complete block of the main flow, though the evidence is from a single user who set up via Claude Code's built-in slash command.

source_issues.title: Claude Code Action won't run due to 'app token exchange' GitHub App installation token (HTTP 401 Unauthorized)
source_issues.evidence: Action exits with code 1 before any Claude API call. OIDC token obtained successfully, but app token exchange fails with 401. Blocks entire workflow from running.

signals.topic: Bun runtime crashes on startup with 'directory mismatch for tsconfig.json' error, preventing any Claude execution
signals.summary: The action consistently crashes immediately on startup with an internal Bun error 'directory mismatch for directory tsconfig.json' before any Claude API call is made. Affects multiple runner images (ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-24.04) and multiple action versions including a pinned SHA that previously succeeded. Error originates from Bun's file descriptor handling when resolving tsconfig.json.
signals.review_reason: Complete main-flow block before any API call. Affects multiple runner images and multiple action versions. p1 label applied by maintainers. Multiple external repository runs linked as evidence. Bun runtime-level crash indicates systemic issue, not user misconfiguration.

source_issues.title: Consistent Bun crash: 'directory mismatch for tsconfig.json' — Claude Code process exits with code 1
source_issues.evidence: Crash occurs before any API call. Tested across ubuntu-22.04/24.04, multiple action versions (v1.0.89, v1.0.90, v1.0.92, pinned SHA). Same SHA that succeeded at 22:22 UTC crashed at 23:03 UTC on same image. p1 label applied by maintainers. Multiple linked failed runs from FliptRx/fliptrx-requirements.

signals.topic: Bedrock authentication broken since v1.0.74 — 'Could not load credentials from any providers' despite valid OIDC credentials
signals.summary: Bedrock users experience 'Could not load credentials from any providers' error immediately after action upgrade to v1.0.74/v1.0.75. OIDC setup (via aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials) works correctly and AWS env vars are present, but the action fails with 0 API tokens consumed, indicating the failure happens before any request is made.
aliases: Could not load credentials from any providers Bedrock
signals.review_reason: p1 label from maintainers indicates high priority. Main flow completely blocked for Bedrock users after a specific version. Zero tokens consumed confirms auth failure before any API call. Clear regression from v1.0.74+.

source_issues.title: Bedrock auth broken since v1.0.74 — 'Could not load credentials from any providers' despite valid OIDC credentials
source_issues.evidence: p1 label applied by maintainers. OIDC step succeeds, AWS env vars confirmed present, but API call never made (0 input/output tokens). Regression from v1.0.74+. Workaround is to pin to older SHA.

signals.topic: Autonomous blockchain token transfers causing irreversible financial loss due to missing safeguards
signals.summary: Claude Code autonomously executed an irreversible ERC20 transfer to a smart contract address without verifying the correct procedure, resulting in $99.88 USDC permanently stuck/lost. No confirmation prompt, no small-amount test, no risk warning was issued.
aliases: Irreversible on-chain fund transfer without confirmation
Unauthorized token transfer leading to permanent financial loss
Blockchain transaction executed without user verification
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point with concrete financial loss evidence: real money ($99.88 USDC) permanently irrecoverable due to Claude Code autonomously executing an irreversible blockchain transaction without user confirmation, risk warning, or verification. This meets the 'obvious cost loss' and 'main flow failure' criteria. The lack of any guardrail (confirmation prompt, small-amount test, risk warning) for irreversible financial operations represents a systemic safety gap affecting any user who delegates blockchain interactions to Claude Code. Priority P0 is justified by the severity of financial harm and irreversibility, despite count=1.

source_issues.title: SAFETY: Claude Code lost user's $0.88 by blindly transferring USDC to a smart contract
source_issues.evidence: Real financial loss of $99.88 USDC on Polygon chain due to autonomous execution of ERC20 transfer() to a contract address without understanding the protocol's actual mechanics. TX: 0xce9d7593288161cd443beb7c2cb3cb7395916628ce1e091a9391e35acff644af. No confirmation, no test transaction, no risk warning was provided.

signals.topic: Desktop app regressions: Dispatch window text uncopyable, copy button missing from responses, Mac keys displayed on Windows
signals.summary: Three desktop UI regressions: (1) Text in Dispatch window cannot be selected or copied — regression from prior build. (2) Copy button lost from hover on assistant responses in desktop app. (3) Mac key symbols shown instead of Windows keys in approval prompts.
signals.review_reason: Multiple desktop UI regressions across platforms. Dispatch window copy is a direct functional regression. Copy button loss and wrong key symbols are visible UX degradations. Count=3 from distinct issues with confirmed reproduction.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Cannot select or copy text from Dispatch window
source_issues.evidence: Text in Dispatch window cannot be selected or copied. No selection highlight on click-drag. Clipboard empty after Cmd+C. Regression from prior desktop build.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Copy response has been lost from new Claude Code
source_issues.evidence: Copy button previously visible on hover next to assistant responses is no longer present. Users cannot copy entire replies with one click.

source_issues.title: [BUG] showing Mac Key-symbols on windows
source_issues.evidence: Windows app displays Mac key symbols (e.g., ⌘) instead of Windows keys (Ctrl) in approval prompts. Key-symbol formatter is not branching on process.platform.

signals.topic: remote-control worktree silently deletes completed session branches and commits on session end — permanent data loss
signals.summary: When using --spawn worktree, all worktree branches and commits are silently deleted when sessions end. No warning, no merge prompt, no git reflog trace. Users lose hours of agent work permanently.
signals.review_reason: P0 despite count=1: explicit data loss with zero recovery path confirmed by user. Worktree, branches, and commits are silently deleted on session end with no reflog entry. Multiple hours of agent work destroyed.

source_issues.title: [BUG] remote-control --spawn worktree silently deletes completed session worktrees and commits on session end
source_issues.evidence: User reports 5 sessions (3 completed ~4h each, 2 failed at rate limit). All work gone — git reflog, git branch, git worktree list show no trace. Hours of agent work permanently lost.

signals.topic: Auto-generated plan slugs collide and silently overwrite existing plans — data corruption and destruction
signals.summary: Plan slugs are random adjective+verb+surname codenames. With many plans, slug collisions silently overwrite existing plans. Slugs used as primary identifiers in commits, chats, and cross-plan links.
signals.review_reason: P0 despite count=1: confirmed silent data destruction via slug collisions. Plan data is silently corrupted/overwritten. Slugs are used as primary cross-references, making the damage widespread and hard to detect.

source_issues.title: Whoever signed off on auto-naming the load-bearing identifier of a document with random adjective+verb+surname owes the world an apology
source_issues.evidence: User reports 140 plans with 137 having auto-generated codenames. Confirmed slug collisions silently overwrite existing plans, destroying data. Slugs are primary identifiers across commits, chats, and cross-plan links.

signals.topic: MCP tools/list pagination (nextCursor) not followed — tools beyond first page silently truncated
signals.summary: Claude Code only fetches the first page of MCP tools. The nextCursor pagination token is silently ignored. Tools beyond the first page are invisible and uncallable, breaking MCP gateways that aggregate tools from multiple servers.
signals.review_reason: Key MCP protocol feature broken — tools silently truncated beyond first page. Breaks multi-server MCP gateway architectures. User cannot access their full tool inventory.

source_issues.title: MCP tools/list pagination (nextCursor) not followed — tools silently truncated
source_issues.evidence: MCP tools beyond first page are invisible and uncallable. Breaks MCP gateways that aggregate tools from multiple servers. User's entire tool inventory is silently incomplete.

signals.topic: Cowork Windows: WebFetch egress proxy blocks all domains regardless of 'All domains' allowlist setting
signals.summary: WebFetch in Cowork Windows returns EGRESS_BLOCKED for every URL even when allowlist is set to 'All domains' and network egress is enabled. Cowork collaboration feature is completely non-functional.
signals.review_reason: Cowork feature completely non-functional on Windows. Every WebFetch request blocked regardless of allowlist settings. Collaboration feature unusable.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Cowork Windows: WebFetch egress proxy blocks all domains regardless of 'All domains' allowlist setting
source_issues.evidence: User reports every URL blocked (en.wikipedia.org, etc.) despite 'All domains' allowlist and enabled egress. Cowork WebFetch feature is completely non-functional.

signals.topic: LLM grading example uses buggy substring matching causing 100% false positive scores
signals.summary: The `grade_completion` function in the LLM-based grading documentation example uses `"correct" in grader_response.lower()` which incorrectly matches 'incorrect' (since 'correct' is a substring of 'incorrect'). This causes every answer to be scored as 'correct', giving 100% score even with intentionally wrong golden answers. The bug is in the official platform documentation and directly breaks the evaluation workflow for developers using this cookbook example.
signals.review_reason: This is a concrete, reproducible bug in official platform documentation that breaks the evaluation workflow. The grading function silently produces 100% accuracy scores even with wrong golden answers because 'correct' is a substring of 'incorrect'. This directly misleads developers who copy the example into their evaluation pipelines, causing false confidence in model performance. The issue provides full reproduction steps and a suggested fix, confirming it is a real workflow-affecting defect.

source_issues.title: [BUG] False positive in LLM-based grading example
source_issues.evidence: The `grade_completion` function uses `"correct" in grader_response.lower()` — since 'correct' is a substring of 'incorrect', every grading result is marked correct. Demo shows a test case with an intentionally wrong golden answer ('The capital of japan is madrid') still scoring 100%.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: inbound messages silently fail to reach Claude Code session
signals.summary: Telegram plugin fails to deliver inbound messages to Claude Code across multiple platforms. The subprocess dies silently during idle, messages are consumed from Telegram API but never bridged as channel tags, and the poll loop permanently exits on non-409 transient errors — leaving the bot completely deaf to inbound messages while outbound tools still appear to work.
aliases: telegram plugin stops receiving messages silently
telegram inbound not bridged to Claude Code
signals.review_reason: 4 independent reports across Linux and Windows confirming the same user impact: inbound Telegram messages silently fail to reach the Claude Code session. Root cause spans multiple failure modes (subprocess death, poll loop exit, message consumption without bridging). This is a primary use-case failure — users cannot receive Telegram messages within their Claude Code session. Verified cross-platform (Linux + Windows).

source_issues.title: [telegram] Plugin subprocess dies silently during idle; CLI doesn't respawn
source_issues.evidence: Telegram plugin dies silently during extended idle/polling. MCP stdio subprocess exits but claude mcp list still reports Connected. No inbound messages reach the session and reply tool calls fail until full CLI restart.

source_issues.title: telegram v0.0.5: inbound messages consumed but not delivered as channel tag (Windows, CC 2.1.101)
source_issues.evidence: On Windows 11, bot successfully receives messages from Telegram API (getUpdates returns empty, pending_update_count=0) but they are never delivered as <channel source=telegram> tags. Reproduces across multiple fresh sessions.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin 0.0.5: inbound messages not bridged to Claude Code (outbound works)
source_issues.evidence: Bot process runs and successfully consumes messages from Telegram API but messages never reach Claude Code input stream. Outbound Claude-to-Telegram via reply tool works fine. Not the zombie-poller issue — only one bot process running, no 409 Conflicts.

source_issues.title: fix(telegram): poll loop exits permanently on non-409 errors — root cause of inbound stops reports
source_issues.evidence: Poll-loop only retries 409 Conflict. Any transient error (connection timeout, TLS reset, DNS hiccup, HTTP 5xx) causes catch block to return permanently. Plugin process stays alive (MCP stdin keeps event loop), outbound tools work but bot is completely deaf to inbound messages.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: zombie bun processes spin at 100% CPU indefinitely on macOS and Linux
signals.summary: After telegram v0.0.5 fix (#1349), orphaned bun server.ts processes from previous sessions continue spinning at 95-100% CPU indefinitely. The orphan watchdog fails to detect dead sessions on macOS/Linux, and the busy-loop inside the poller is not addressed by the 0.0.5 fix. Causes significant resource consumption and machine heating.
signals.review_reason: 3 reports (including 2 distinct reports of zombie processes spinning at 100% CPU on macOS and Linux after the v0.0.5 patch). The 0.0.5 fix addressed zombie handover but not the underlying busy-loop in the poller. Causes sustained high CPU usage and machine heating. Clear user impact (resource consumption, hardware damage risk).

source_issues.title: telegram: orphan watchdog ineffective -- zombie bun processes spin at 100% CPU
source_issues.evidence: Orphan watchdog added in v0.0.5 fails to detect dead sessions on macOS. Orphaned bun server.ts processes spin at ~100% CPU indefinitely on broken MCP stdin pipe. Two zombies observed running 23h and 4h at ~98% CPU each, heating the machine significantly.

source_issues.title: [telegram] server.ts pegs 100% CPU per zombie poller despite 0.0.5 fix (#1349)
source_issues.evidence: Zombie bun server.ts processes spin at ~95-100% CPU per process. The 0.0.5 fix handles handover (kill-stale-on-startup, retry on 409, force-exit on shutdown) but does not address the underlying busy-loop inside the poller itself.

source_issues.title: [telegram] server.ts pegs 100% CPU per zombie poller despite 0.0.5 fix (#1349)
source_issues.evidence: Same issue as #1384: zombie bun server.ts processes from telegram plugin spin at 95-100% CPU. The 0.0.5 fix does not address the underlying busy-loop inside the poller.

signals.topic: security-guidance hook outputs plain text instead of JSON causing hook system to fail
signals.summary: The security-guidance plugin's PreToolUse hook outputs plain text to stderr when blocking a tool use, but Claude Code's hook system expects JSON format output. This causes 'hook json output validation failed' error on every trigger, breaking the hook entirely — the security reminder never displays and the block is ineffective.
aliases: hook json output validation failed security-guidance
signals.review_reason: Single report but the bug completely breaks the security-guidance hook's core functionality. The hook outputs plain text instead of required JSON, causing validation failure on every trigger — meaning the security reminder block never works at all. This defeats the entire purpose of the security-guidance plugin, which is a critical safety feature.

source_issues.title: security-guidance hook outputs plain text instead of JSON, causing json output validation error
source_issues.evidence: security-guidance plugin PreToolUse hook uses print(reminder, file=sys.stderr) + sys.exit(2) instead of outputting JSON. Claude Code hook system requires JSON format. Result: hook json output validation failed on every trigger — the security block is completely ineffective.

signals.topic: remember plugin produces no memory output on Windows due to missing jq dependency
signals.summary: The remember plugin (v0.1.0) does not produce any memory output on Windows. The .remember/ directory stays empty across sessions despite the plugin being enabled and SessionStart/PostToolUse hooks firing. Root cause is a missing jq dependency and slug computation issue on Windows.
aliases: remember plugin not working Windows jq
signals.review_reason: Single-platform (Windows) issue but completely breaks the remember plugin's core memory functionality. The .remember/ directory stays empty so users cannot retrieve past memories. jq is not bundled with the plugin and is not standard on Windows, making this a packaging/release failure that blocks a primary feature.

source_issues.title: remember plugin broken on Windows: jq dependency + slug computation
source_issues.evidence: remember plugin v0.1.0 produces no memory output on Windows. .remember/ stays empty across sessions despite plugin being enabled and hooks firing. Root cause: jq dependency missing on Windows + slug computation fails.

signals.topic: Tutorial content uses retired model (Claude Haiku 3), making exercises non-functional for learners
signals.summary: The interactive tutorial references Claude Haiku 3, a recently-retired model, causing learners to follow code paths for a model that no longer produces the expected outputs. This directly blocks the primary learning flow.
signals.review_reason: The tutorial's primary learning flow is blocked because learners execute code targeting a retired model that no longer produces expected results. While count=1, the review_reason provides strong user impact evidence: a retired model in a learning tutorial means the entire exercise path is non-functional, which is a direct experience degradation for every learner who follows it.

source_issues.title: Tutorial using Haiku 3- needs update
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports the tutorial still uses the recently-retired Claude Haiku 3 and needs updating to Haiku 4.5, preventing learners from running functional code.

signals.topic: XML tags not reflected in tutorial cell outputs, causing misleading lesson content
signals.summary: In the 'Separating_Data_and_Instructions' lesson, the cells that claim to demonstrate XML tags produce output identical to previous cells, meaning the tags are not actually applied. Learners cannot verify their work and receive incorrect visual confirmation.
aliases: Missing XML tag output in tutorial cells
Incorrect output in XML instruction lesson
signals.review_reason: A core lesson step produces silently incorrect output — the XML tags are missing but the cell runs without error, giving learners false confidence that they applied the technique correctly. This is a workflow runtime issue where the tutorial looks functional but teaches incorrect behavior, directly degrading the learning experience for anyone working through the lesson.

source_issues.title: XML tags missing in 04_Separating_Data_and_Instructions
source_issues.evidence: User reports that no XML tags were actually added in the cells about adding XML tags, and the output was identical to the previous (incorrect) cell, making it impossible to verify the lesson step worked as intended.

signals.topic: Name collisions in claude-api skill cause silent file overwrites during skill installation
signals.summary: Five distinct filename collisions in the claude-api skill (claude-api.md, tool-use.md, streaming.md, files-api.md, batches.md) cause files to silently overwrite each other when installed to a flat namespace. Additionally, a YAML parse error in SKILL.md frontmatter breaks installation.
aliases: YAML parse error in claude-api SKILL.md
signals.review_reason: Files silently overwrite each other during skill installation — users lose access to language-specific API documentation without any warning. The YAML parse error further prevents proper installation. This is a clear packaging defect that causes content loss and installation failures.

source_issues.title: Structural lint findings: name collisions in claude-api skill
source_issues.evidence: 5 name collisions across claude-api skill cause silent file overwrites; linter (claude-skill-lint v0.5.1) reports 14 errors across 37 files. Also YAML parse error in SKILL.md frontmatter.

signals.topic: document-skills and example-skills load 17 identical skills — duplicate context waste and routing ambiguity
signals.summary: When both document-skills and example-skills plugins are enabled (the default), they reference the same source directory and load the exact same 17 skills twice under different prefixes. This wastes context tokens and causes routing confusion when Claude tries to select the correct skill.
signals.review_reason: Default behavior after installing the marketplace causes 17 skills to be loaded twice in every conversation. This directly wastes context tokens (a tangible cost for users on token-based plans) and creates routing ambiguity where Claude may unpredictably pick the wrong skill prefix for a given task.

source_issues.title: document-skills and example-skills load identical 17 skills — duplicate context waste
source_issues.evidence: Both plugins in marketplace.json reference the same source directory. Cache directories have identical file counts (376 files) and content hash. 17 skills are loaded twice with different prefixes, wasting context and causing routing ambiguity.

signals.topic: View tool silently truncates skill-creator example skill at ~16K chars — model works from incomplete instructions
signals.summary: The skill-creator example skill is 33,168 characters but the view tool silently truncates at ~16,000 characters without warning. Any model loading this skill via the view tool works from an incomplete copy, missing the core eval/iteration workflow section entirely.
signals.review_reason: The view tool silently cuts the skill-creator in half, leaving the model without the core eval/iteration workflow — which the skill itself identifies as its most important contribution. This is a repeated workflow failure: every user who triggers the skill-creator skill on claude.ai gets a degraded experience with no warning that the skill is incomplete.

source_issues.title: skill-creator example skill exceeds view tool truncation limit by 2x
source_issues.evidence: The skill-creator skill is 33,168 characters. The view tool silently truncates at ~16,000 characters. The core eval/iteration workflow (lines 113-373) is in the truncated middle section. The model using skill-creator on claude.ai works from incomplete instructions with no warning.

signals.topic: MCP user elicitation broken with custom MCP servers (no buttons, no default selection, session crash)
signals.summary: User elicitation in custom MCP servers (FastMCP v3.2.0) is broken: accept/reject buttons do not render, dropdowns lack default selection forcing manual re-selection, and after submission the session crashes with 'Failed to Load Session'.
signals.review_reason: User-facing MCP tool interaction is completely broken. Three distinct sub-failures: (1) no UI buttons → user cannot interact with approval flows, (2) no default selection → validation loop, (3) post-submit session crash → session becomes inaccessible. Blocks any workflow relying on MCP-elicited user input.

source_issues.title: User elicitation does not function correctly with custom MCP server
source_issues.evidence: Accept/reject buttons do not appear in UI (timeout required); first dropdown value not selected by default causing 'This field is required' error; after submission 'Failed to Load Session' crash occurs and chat becomes inaccessible.

signals.topic: Custom OpenAI-compatible provider constructs requests with empty/relative URL causing 404 failures
signals.summary: When using a custom OpenAI-type provider with a valid base_url and API key, goose constructs requests to a blank/relative URL path instead of the configured endpoint, causing all message requests to fail with 404.
signals.review_reason: Complete main-flow failure for custom provider users. Every message request fails with 404 due to malformed URL. The session initializes successfully masking the underlying issue until the user attempts actual interaction. Blocks any workflow using a non-built-in OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

source_issues.title: Custom OpenAI provider 404 with empty URL (opencode.ai zen/go/v1)
source_issues.evidence: Session starts successfully but sending any message triggers 404 error with empty URL — goose is constructing a request to a relative path with no host. Same base_url + API key works via curl. Blocks all custom OpenAI-compatible provider usage.

signals.topic: Context Length Exceeded error causes session crash on fresh install with large local models (Gemma-4-26B)
signals.summary: On a fresh install and first session, using the Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF model causes a Context Length Exceeded error and crashes the session. Subsequent attempts reproduce the crash. Switching to a smaller model (Llama-3.2-3B) resolves it.
aliases: context length exceeded crash on first session
signals.review_reason: Hard crash blocking the primary usage flow (chat interaction) on fresh install with a legitimate model. User captures two crash diagnostics and reproducible failure across multiple attempts. Though single-issue, the severity is high: it renders the application unusable until the user manually identifies and switches to a different model, which requires domain knowledge.

source_issues.title: Context Length Exceeded Error On Fresh Install and First Session
source_issues.evidence: Fresh install, first session with Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF: Context Length Exceeded error displayed, then session crashes. Repeating the question reproduces the crash. Attaching two crash diagnostics bundles. Switching to Llama-3.2-3B works correctly.

signals.topic: Deleted chat sessions remain in sidebar as stale entries, causing 'Session not found' errors on click

aliases: session cache not invalidated in sidebar
signals.review_reason: State synchronization bug between two UI views causes a misleading error state. The stale entry leads users to believe a session exists when it does not, producing a non-recoverable error (toast persists, no retry mechanism) until app restart. Degrades trust in session management UI.

source_issues.title: [UI] Deleted chat session still appears in sidebar list (stale cache) and shows 'Session not found' when clicked
source_issues.evidence: After deleting a session from Show All view, the entry remains in the sidebar. Clicking the stale entry shows 'Failed to Load Session — Session <id> not found' error. Only app restart refreshes the list. Screenshot evidence provided.

signals.topic: Mermaid diagram rendering stuck in 'Waiting for data' on Windows (behind proxy)

source_issues.title: Mermaid rendering stuck in Waiting for data status

signals.topic: Silent exception swallowing across 66 code locations causes agents to silently fail without user signal
signals.summary: Static analysis found 66 instances of `except Exception: pass` / `except Exception: return None` in core modules including memory, reasoning handler, and tool systems. Agents silently fail — memory writes that fail are lost, reasoning steps that fail are omitted, and tool calls that error produce no output — leaving users with incorrect results and no indication of failure.
signals.review_reason: Code quality defect with documented user impact: silent error masking in core modules means agents silently produce wrong outputs. In an AI agent framework, agents continuing with incorrect internal state (failed memory writes, failed reasoning steps, failed tool calls) without any user-visible signal is a critical UX failure. Not marked P0 only because count=1 — a single issue with a sweeping code pattern across 66 locations is more of a systemic quality problem than a single-blocker event.

signals.topic: InternalInstructor discards base_url — breaks all OpenAI-compatible self-hosted endpoints (vLLM, Ollama, etc.)
signals.summary: InternalInstructor._create_instructor_client() extracts only the model name from the LLM object, ignoring the base_url entirely. When users configure OpenAI-compatible providers with custom endpoints (vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, etc.), the instructor client silently ignores the base_url and calls api.openai.com instead. A workaround via _get_llm_extra_kwargs() exists but only activates for LiteLLM providers.
signals.review_reason: Breaks a core integration pattern for self-hosted LLM users. base_url is silently ignored, causing converter/internal instructor features to call api.openai.com instead of the user's configured endpoint. This means: (1) users pay for OpenAI API calls they didn't intend, (2) self-hosted models are never called, (3) data is sent to OpenAI without user consent. Cost impact + privacy impact.

source_issues.title: [BUG] InternalInstructor discards base_url when creating instructor client — breaks OpenAI-compatible endpoints

Affects all non-LiteLLM OpenAI-compatible providers (vLLM, Ollama, self-hosted). _get_llm_extra_kwargs() forwards base_url but is only active for is_litellm=True.
