source_issues.title: Gemini-2.5-pro hangs in interactive mode and fails with MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED
source_issues.evidence: On Windows, gemini-2.5-pro request fails with 429 and MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED, looping without surfacing error to user.

source_issues.title: Great delays and finally acceso denied
source_issues.evidence: User paying €40/month for combined subscription cannot access preview models. Receives access denied error with no clear recovery path.

signals.topic: Terminal display instability during active streaming: erratic scrolling/jumping and screen flickering
signals.summary: During streaming of model output (thoughts, answers, work-in-progress updates), the terminal viewport exhibits two related problems: (1) erratic jumping/scrolling that unpredictably moves to top or auto-scrolls to bottom, making it impossible to read previous output, and (2) aggressive screen flickering/blinking in the bottom portion of the terminal. These behaviors are disruptive to productivity and potentially harmful for users sensitive to screen flashes.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct reports of terminal display instability during active streaming. The scrolling/jumping issue makes it 'exceptionally difficult' to track interaction history (core UX degradation). The blinking issue explicitly raises a health concern about epilepsy triggers. Both are reproducible, user-visible, and affect the primary interaction loop.

source_issues.title: Similar terminal scrolling/jumping behavior observed with Gemini CLI
source_issues.evidence: During active output, terminal viewport jumps to top or auto-scrolls to bottom unpredictably. Makes reading and tracking previous messages 'exceptionally difficult', 'disrupting the flow of interaction'. References similar known issue in claude-code.

source_issues.title: Screen is blinking during active usage in terminal
source_issues.evidence: Screen bottom blinks during intensive work-in-progress streaming and typing simultaneously. Video attached. Explicitly raises health concern: 'may affect user health... up to triggering epilepsy episodes'.

source_issues.title: Debug Console error
source_issues.evidence: Debug console flickering on screen during 429 error, compounding the UI disruption during rate-limited streaming.

signals.topic: Agent hangs indefinitely with no progress feedback, causing multi-hour stalls
signals.summary: Users report the agent getting stuck for hours with zero feedback or progress indication, spinning in 'Thinking...' state indefinitely. Two distinct users on different OS/platforms (FreeBSD and Windows) experienced the agent hanging with no response, with one lasting 3 hours on a small build log review task. The agent shows no activity, no status update, and no error — just silence.
aliases: Agent gets stuck for hours with no feedback
Spins for hours with no status update
signals.review_reason: Agent indefinite hangs block the primary workflow. Two distinct users on different platforms independently reported multi-hour stalls with zero feedback. This is a main-flow blocking issue — the agent becomes completely unusable for extended periods without any user action to recover other than manual cancellation.

source_issues.title: Not doing anything for 3 hours after giving it a small build log
source_issues.evidence: Agent spun for 3 hours with no feedback when asked to review a build failure. No status update, no activity — user was completely blocked.

source_issues.title: Insanely Long thinking time
source_issues.evidence: Agent stuck in 'Thinking...' state indefinitely. Screenshot attached showing prolonged hang. Explicitly described as stuck.

signals.topic: macOS quarantine attribute blocks downloaded rg binary, preventing agent from running on macOS
signals.summary: On macOS, the ripgrep (rg) binary downloaded by Gemini CLI is tagged with the com.apple.quarantine extended attribute. This causes macOS Gatekeeper to block execution of rg, preventing the Gemini coding agent from functioning. Users must manually run xattr -d com.apple.quarantine to unblock. This is a recurring issue when the CLI downloads or updates tool binaries.
signals.review_reason: count=1 (single repo), so default P2 applies per rules. However, review_reason notes this is a reproducible blocking issue on macOS where the agent cannot run the rg tool without manual intervention. The workaround is non-obvious (requires knowledge of xattr) and affects every macOS user who uses the coding agent. While count<3, the user impact is clear and blocking. Elevated to P1 consideration due to complete agent blockage on affected OS.

source_issues.title: Quarantined version of ripgrep (rg) on macOS
source_issues.evidence: User hitting quarantine error when Gemini coding agent tries to use ripgrep on macOS. xattr confirmed quarantine attribute present on downloaded rg binary. Workaround requires manual xattr removal. Known similar issue in Zed IDE.

signals.topic: VisitWebpageTool fails on Cloudflare-protected sites, causing silent research quality degradation
signals.summary: smolagents' built-in VisitWebpageTool silently returns empty content on a large fraction of web URLs protected by Cloudflare, directly degrading research agent output quality without any user-facing error or warning.
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: the core web scraping tool silently fails on Cloudflare-protected sites, degrading research agent quality on a large fraction of URLs. No error is surfaced to the user — it returns empty content without warning, so the user cannot even know their agent is working with incomplete data. This directly impacts the primary use case (web research agents) and causes silent data quality loss. Count=1 and single repo, so P2, not P0.

source_issues.title: Tool suggestion: anybrowse for web scraping with Cloudflare bypass
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states 'smolagents VisitWebpageTool fails on Cloudflare-protected sites. For research agents this silently degrades quality -- empty content on a large fraction of useful URLs.'

signals.topic: Deploy bundler missing runtime dependencies for 10 of 16 model providers — silent ImportError after successful deploy
signals.summary: When deploying with 10 different model providers (fireworks, together, deepseek, etc.), the bundler validation passes and deploy exits 0, but the generated agent bundle is missing the required langchain-* package, causing ImportError at runtime when the agent starts.
aliases: bundler missing deps for model providers
missing langchain provider packages in deploy bundle
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：用户完成 deploy 配置、凭证验证通过、部署命令正常退出，但生成的 agent 在启动时立即崩溃，直接阻断所有使用受影响 model provider 的用户。证据确凿（10/16 providers affected，包括 fireworks/deepseek/together 等常用 provider），两次独立 issue 均提供完整复现步骤，属于打包配置级缺陷而非用户配置错误。

source_issues.title: Deploy bundler missing deps for 10 of 16 model providers — silent ImportError at runtime
source_issues.evidence: 10 providers (fireworks, baseten, together, xai, nvidia, cohere, deepseek, openrouter, perplexity, azure_openai) are absent from _MODEL_PROVIDER_DEPS in bundler.py. Config validation passes (API keys checked), deploy exits 0, agent crashes at runtime with ImportError. Reproducer: set FIREWORKS_API_KEY, run deepagents deploy with model=fireworks:..., deploy succeeds, agent starts, crashes with 'No module named langchain_fireworks'.

source_issues.title: deploy: together provider not bundled — ImportError at runtime
source_issues.evidence: Specific reproducer for 'together' provider: TOGETHER_API_KEY is validated in _MODEL_PROVIDER_ENV, deepagents deploy exits 0, but generated pyproject.toml lacks langchain-together, causing 'ImportError: No module named langchain_together' when agent starts.

signals.topic: config.toml params.api_key 被 create_model() 凭证早期检查忽略 — 用户正确配置仍报无凭证错误
signals.summary: create_model() 在加载 config.toml 参数之前执行凭证检查，导致即使 params.api_key 已正确配置在 config.toml 中，has_provider_credentials() 仍返回 False 并抛出 ModelConfigError。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：用户按照文档正确配置 config.toml 中的 params.api_key，CLI 启动后立即失败，要求设置环境变量，体验与文档严重不符。两条独立 issue 来自不同报告者，均提供完整复现步骤，根因定位清晰（检查顺序错误）。

source_issues.title: Bug: create_model() early credential check ignores params.api_key from config.toml
source_issues.evidence: create_model() raises ModelConfigError: 'No credentials found for provider litellm' even when params.api_key is correctly set in config.toml. Root cause: early credential check in config.py L2241-2249 runs before _get_provider_kwargs() loads params from config file. has_provider_credentials() only checks api_key_env field and hardcoded PROVIDER_API_KEY_ENV map, not params.api_key.

source_issues.title: Bug: create_model() early credential check ignores params.api_key from config.toml
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #2724 with more detailed root cause analysis. Demonstrates that params.api_key from config is a documented and valid credential source that is silently ignored by the early credential check.

signals.topic: PatchToolCallsMiddleware 不处理 invalid_tool_calls — token 溢出截断后触发 BadRequestError 阻断 agent 运行
signals.summary: 当模型输出因 token 溢出被截断导致 JSON 格式错误时，msg.invalid_tool_calls 包含无法修复的工具调用，但 PatchToolCallsMiddleware 仅遍历 msg.tool_calls，导致 API 返回 400 BadRequestError，agent 完全停止运行。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：agent 在特定 token 溢出场景下触发不可恢复的 400 API 错误，agent.invoke() 完全停止。用户已定位根因（middleware 未处理 invalid_tool_calls）并验证修复有效，属于 middleware 逻辑缺陷。

source_issues.title: PatchToolCallsMiddleware cannot handle msg.invalid_tool_calls without ToolMessage
source_issues.evidence: When agent.invoke() triggers a token overflow and JSON truncation, msg.invalid_tool_calls is populated. PatchToolCallsMiddleware only iterates msg.tool_calls (not msg.invalid_tool_calls), causing the API to return BadRequestError: 'An assistant message with tool_calls must be followed by tool messages responding to each tool_call_id'. User debugged the issue in source and confirmed the fix: changing the loop to include msg.invalid_tool_calls resolves the error.

signals.topic: Subgraph tools not found — /threads/{thread_id}/history 端点抛出 ValueError 导致历史记录不可用
signals.summary: 使用 create_deep_agent 创建含自定义 @tool 的 agent 后，调用 GET /threads/{thread_id}/history 时抛出 ValueError: Subgraph tools not found，因为 deepagents 将 tool 编译为子图节点写入 checkpoint，但未通过 aget_subgraphs() 正确暴露给 LangGraph runtime。
aliases: checkpoint restore fails for custom tools
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：history 端点是 agent 持久化对话的核心功能，带自定义 tool 的 agent 在生成 checkpoint 后无法通过 history 端点恢复历史，直接影响多轮对话和状态恢复场景。错误堆栈指向 LangGraph 内部，根因分析指向 deepagents 子图注册问题。

source_issues.title: Subgraph tools not found when calling /threads/{thread_id}/history
source_issues.evidence: After creating agent with custom @tool and running one conversation to generate checkpoint, calling GET /threads/{thread_id}/history throws ValueError: 'Subgraph tools not found' at langgraph/pregel/main.py line 1436 in aget_state_history. Root cause: deepagents compiles tools into a 'tools' subgraph node and writes to checkpoint, but this subgraph is not properly exposed via aget_subgraphs() to the LangGraph runtime, causing state history reconstruction to fail.

signals.topic: ACP 插件启用失败 — deepagents-acp 已安装仍报 ImportError 导致 ACP 功能完全不可用
signals.summary: 用户通过 uv tool install deepagents-cli --with deepagents-acp 安装了 ACP 依赖，但 deepagents --acp 仍报 cannot import name SessionConfigOption from acp.schema，ACP 功能完全无法使用。
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：ACP 功能为 deepagents 的核心插件系统，用户按正确方式安装后完全无法启用，报错指向包间版本兼容性问题，有具体 ImportError 堆栈和文件路径证据，属于打包/依赖版本问题。

source_issues.title: Cannot enable acp with deepagents-cli
source_issues.evidence: User installs deepagents-acp via 'uv tool install deepagents-cli --with deepagents-acp', but 'deepagents --acp' still raises ImportError: cannot import name 'SessionConfigOption' from 'acp.schema'. The schema.py file exists at the expected path, suggesting a version mismatch or import path issue between the ACP package and deepagents.

signals.topic: default_tool_parser crashes on malformed function dicts, silently drops all valid tool calls
signals.summary: When any single tool call in a streaming response has a malformed function dict (None or missing keys), the entire parsing loop raises TypeError/KeyError, causing ALL tool calls—including valid ones—to be silently dropped. No error is surfaced to the user.
aliases: Tool call parsing failure with malformed input
Streaming tool parser silently drops all tool calls on one malformed call
signals.review_reason: Critical main flow failure: ANY malformed tool call in streaming response causes entire tool calling system to silently fail. Users lose ALL tool functionality for that response without error indication. Unacceptable for production agents relying on tool calls.

source_issues.title: core: default_tool_parser crashes on malformed function dicts, silently drops all valid tool calls
source_issues.evidence: TypeError/KeyError when function field is None or missing keys. One malformed call kills entire parsing loop. ALL tool calls including valid ones are silently dropped due to broad exception handling in caller. Malformed dicts never reach invalid_tool_calls list despite existing for this purpose.

signals.topic: _batch and _abatch lack batch_size validation causing infinite loop or endless empty batches
signals.summary: Synchronous _batch with batch_size=0 enters an infinite while loop. Asynchronous _abatch with batch_size=0 yields empty lists indefinitely instead of erroring. Both degrade silently with no user-facing error.
aliases: Indexing batch utilities hang with zero/negative size
_abatch yields empty batches indefinitely with zero size
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure causing infinite loops or endless iteration with zero batch_size. Silent performance degradation with _abatch (empty batches instead of error). Users lose hours debugging hangs or waste CPU on meaningless empty batch processing. Common indexing functionality affected.

source_issues.title: bug(core): _batch and _abatch lack batch_size validation causing infinite loop
source_issues.evidence: Synchronous _batch(0, data) enters infinite while loop. Asynchronous _abatch(0, data) yields empty lists for every element indefinitely. Both hang or degrade silently without error. Proposed fix: validate size > 0 at function start.

signals.topic: Silent exception swallowing, unbounded caches, uncontrolled thread creation, and connection leaks across multiple components
signals.summary: 12 instances of silent exception swallowing in tools/core/partner SDKs. Unbounded LRU cache in tokenizer and unbounded global _LOGGED set in tracers cause memory leaks. 5 uncontrolled thread creations in shell_tool and huggingface pipeline. 2 connection lifecycle leaks in sql_record_manager and entity memory.
aliases: Silent error handling causing hidden failures
signals.review_reason: Multiple resource management issues affecting long-running agents: silent failures mask data corruption, unbounded caches consume memory indefinitely, uncontrolled threads exhaust system resources under load, connection leaks degrade service over time. Systematic reliability issue across multiple components.

source_issues.title: Code quality: silent exception swallowing, unbounded caches, thread safety, and connection leaks
source_issues.evidence: 12 instances of silent exception swallowing (tools core, serialization, partner SDKs). Unbounded lru_cache in tokenizer. Unbounded global _LOGGED set in tracers. 5 uncontrolled thread creations in shell_tool and huggingface pipeline. 2 connection lifecycle leaks in sql_record_manager and entity memory. Static analysis findings from HefestoAI tool.

signals.topic: ShellSession hangs until timeout when command stdout lacks trailing newline and done marker is appended to same line
signals.summary: Commands like printf without trailing newline cause ShellSession to hang indefinitely until timeout, because the done marker detection fails when appended to the same line as command output.
aliases: ShellSession hangs on commands without trailing newline
signals.review_reason: ShellSession hangs indefinitely until timeout for common shell commands like printf without newlines. Users lose agent execution time waiting for artificial timeout. Affects main shell tool functionality with predictable reproduction.

source_issues.title: ShellSession times out when stdout has no trailing newline and the done marker is appended to the same line
source_issues.evidence: CommandExecutionResult(output='', exit_code=None, timed_out=True, ...) instead of expected output='hello without newline'. Root cause: printf marker detection fails when command output lacks trailing newline, causing commands to hang until timeout.

signals.topic: _create_usage_metadata crashes with TypeError when OpenAI service_tier is set and cached_tokens is missing
signals.summary: Using OpenAI priority/flex service_tier without cached_tokens causes TypeError in _create_usage_metadata because .get() returns None instead of 0 for existing keys.
aliases: OpenAI usage metadata crash with service_tier
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure when using OpenAI priority/flex service tiers. Users encounter TypeError during usage metadata processing with no workaround. Affects cost tracking and monitoring features for production deployments using service tiers.

source_issues.title: bug(openai): _create_usage_metadata crashes with TypeError when service_tier is set and cached_tokens is missing
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'int' and 'NoneType' when service_tier='priority' or 'flex' and cached_tokens is absent. Dict stores None via .get() and .get(key, 0) returns None (not 0) because key exists. Related to #36500 which fixed same pattern elsewhere.

signals.topic: AsyncPostgresSaver uses threading.Lock under async execution, causing 6x throughput degradation in high-concurrency environments
signals.summary: AsyncPostgresSaver enforces an instance-level threading.Lock() that serializes all async cursor operations, reducing throughput from ~1295 req/s (unlocked baseline) to ~200 req/s in production benchmarks against Cloud SQL PostgreSQL. The lock prevents concurrent asyncio tasks from utilizing the underlying AsyncConnectionPool.
signals.review_reason: Clear production benchmark evidence: AsyncPostgresSaver serializes all async checkpoint operations via threading.Lock, causing 6x throughput collapse. High-concurrency FastAPI+LangGraph deployments on Cloud SQL PostgreSQL are directly impacted with no workaround besides abandoning the checkpointer.

source_issues.title: AsyncPostgresSaver enforces instance-level threading.Lock() during asynchronous execution
source_issues.evidence: Load test benchmark comparing locked vs unlocked baseline shows 6x throughput degradation (1295 req/s baseline vs 200 req/s with AsyncPostgresSaver) on identical Cloud SQL PostgreSQL infrastructure with max_size=100 connection pool. Throughput bottlenecked locally by Python threading.Lock rather than DB capacity.

signals.topic: ensure_config mutates shared metadata dict by reference, leaking thread_id and configurable values across invocations
signals.summary: ensure_config() assigns the metadata key by reference without calling .copy(), causing thread_id values from previous invocations to contaminate the shared base config metadata. After first invocation, subsequent calls see previous thread_id values injected into the base metadata dict.
aliases: thread_id leaks into base config metadata
signals.review_reason: Core API correctness bug: ensure_config silently mutates the base config metadata dict by reference, causing cross-thread state contamination. After first agent invocation with a thread_id, subsequent invocations inherit the previous thread_id in their base metadata. Directly breaks thread isolation guarantees fundamental to LangGraph's checkpointing model.

source_issues.title: bug: ensure_config mutates shared metadata when copiable keys passed by reference
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible example shows original_config metadata dict is mutated after ensure_config call: {'ls_integration': 'langchain_create_agent', 'thread_id': 'thread-1'}. Expected metadata to remain {'ls_integration': 'langchain_create_agent'}. Thread contamination confirmed via assertion failure.

signals.topic: Agent infinite loops until recursion limit error after tool call failures, with no graceful recovery
signals.summary: Agent loops indefinitely calling the same tool after it fails, exhausting the recursion limit. Tool results are cached but the agent ignores them and retries the same failing call. Works correctly on langgraph 0.6* versions.
aliases: Text-to-SQL agent loops on tool error
signals.review_reason: Agent main loop is broken in version 1.0.6: after a tool call fails with a SQL error, the agent ignores the error and retries the same tool 8+ times within seconds, hitting recursion limit. This blocks the main agent workflow entirely and was not reproducible in 0.6* versions, confirming a regression.

source_issues.title: LangGraph [1.0.6] Bug - Agent infinite looping until recursion limit error is hit
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace from production shows agent calling query_databricks tool 8 times in ~16 seconds after receiving SQLSTATE 42K05 error. Recursion limit of 20 reached after ~1 minute. User confirms same code works on langgraph 0.6* version. Tool results cached but agent retries anyway.

signals.topic: add_messages(format='langchain-openai') silently strips message IDs and additional_kwargs on every reducer call
signals.summary: The _format_messages() function calls convert_to_openai_messages() without include_id=True, causing message IDs to be set to None and custom additional_kwargs to be silently dropped on every add_messages call. This breaks ID-based deduplication and loses custom UI/metadata stored in additional_kwargs.
aliases: add_messages strips message IDs langchain-openai format
message ID lost in OpenAI format round-trip
signals.review_reason: Message IDs are silently set to None and custom additional_kwargs are silently dropped on every add_messages call using format='langchain-openai'. This silently breaks ID-based deduplication and update logic on every reducer invocation, with no error raised. Affects all users who use the OpenAI message format in LangGraph.

source_issues.title: bug: add_messages(format="langchain-openai") strips message IDs and additional_kwargs
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible example shows HumanMessage(id='msg-1') results in result[0].id = None after add_messages with format='langchain-openai'. additional_kwargs containing custom widget data is also silently dropped to {}. No error is raised, data loss is silent.

signals.topic: TAG_NOSTREAM tag only suppresses LLM tokens but not node output messages in stream_mode='messages'
signals.summary: StreamMessagesHandler checks TAG_NOSTREAM only in on_chat_model_start but not in on_chain_start, causing node output messages to leak through the stream even when tagged nostream. Downstream frameworks (CopilotKit, Deep Agents) rely on TAG_NOSTREAM for per-subagent streaming control.
aliases: nostream tag leaks node output messages
signals.review_reason: TAG_NOSTREAM is inconsistently applied: it suppresses LLM tokens in on_chat_model_start but node output messages still stream via on_chain_start. This breaks per-subagent streaming control for frameworks built on LangGraph (Deep Agents, CopilotKit) and causes unwanted messages to appear in client streams.

source_issues.title: `TAG_NOSTREAM` inconsistency in `StreamMessagesHandler`: suppresses LLM tokens but not node output messages
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible example shows 'silent' node with tags=['nostream'] still emits AIMessage content to the stream despite TAG_NOSTREAM tag. Downstream impact on langchain-ai/deepagents#2702 and CopilotKit/CopilotKit#3861 confirmed.

signals.topic: Workspace policy fail-open: unauthorized operations possible when policy service fails
signals.summary: When enterprise workspace policy service errors (non-Forbidden exceptions), the code logs the error and proceeds with invite/owner-transfer operations instead of denying them, creating a fail-open authorization bypass.
aliases: workspace policy permission bypass on service error
signals.review_reason: This is a real authorization fail-open design flaw. When the enterprise policy service is unavailable (timeout, exception), workspace invite and owner-transfer operations bypass permission checks and execute anyway. While count=1, the security implication is significant — unauthorized workspace membership operations can be performed under failure conditions. This meets the bar for user pain point (security-critical path with clear exploit scenario) even as a single issue.

source_issues.title: Refactor: fail-closed handling for workspace policy permission checks
source_issues.evidence: API allows invite/owner-transfer operations to proceed when enterprise policy lookup raises non-Forbidden exceptions. User with elevated workspace permissions can potentially perform unauthorized membership operations if the backend policy service fails or times out.

signals.topic: Login page infinite reload loop blocks user authentication
signals.summary: Self-hosted users accessing /signin encounter an infinite reload loop, making login impossible without manually canceling the browser request.
signals.review_reason: Primary authentication flow is completely blocked for self-hosted users. The login page reloads indefinitely and credentials cannot be entered. This is a core user flow failure with no workaround in the affected deployments. Despite count=1, the user impact is severe enough to warrant P0.

source_issues.title: Before login /signin loops reloading if not interrupted manually
source_issues.evidence: Accessing /signin triggers an infinite reload loop in v1.13.3 self-hosted (Source). Users cannot enter credentials without manually stopping the loop via browser 'cancel' button. Both self-hosted Source and Docker deployments affected. Blocks primary authentication flow.

signals.topic: New app creation results in indefinite loading — Studio app editor inaccessible
signals.summary: Creating a new blank app from the dashboard opens Studio but the app never finishes initializing, leaving the processing indicator spinning indefinitely and blocking all editing.
aliases: new app never loads in studio
signals.review_reason: Primary workflow (app creation/editing) is completely blocked. The new app creation flow renders the Studio editor unusable with an indefinite spinner. No functional editing is possible on newly created apps. Workaround of importing DSL is not acceptable for normal usage. Despite count=1, this is a core productivity blocker.

source_issues.title: When creating new app, app is not fully initialized.
source_issues.evidence: Creating a new app from blank in v1.13.3 causes Studio to show indefinite processing indicator. App editing is completely blocked. Workaround: import a blank app via DSL. Reported by same user as #35168 (login loop), both appear to share a root cause affecting the frontend initialization chain.

signals.topic: Streaming response crashes with ChunkedEncodingError — response ends prematurely
signals.summary: When using Python SDK with response_mode=streaming on chatflow, the connection drops mid-stream with ChunkedEncodingError instead of returning error information.
signals.review_reason: A core API usage path (streaming mode via Python SDK) throws an unhandled ChunkedEncodingError that crashes the client. The user receives no structured error response — only an exception. This affects SDK-based integrations and represents a significant degradation for streaming use cases.

source_issues.title: Response ended prematurely when response_mode is streaming
source_issues.evidence: Python SDK call to chatflow with response_mode=streaming raises 'requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError: Response ended prematurely'. The same flow with response_mode=blocking returns a 400 error. Users relying on streaming mode get an unhandled exception rather than a structured error response.

signals.topic: Agent tool call details not persisted in logs — debugging complex flows impossible
signals.summary: Agent tool call parameters, responses, and execution status are not saved in logs; they disappear after the thinking phase ends, making post-hoc debugging of failed tool calls impossible.
aliases: agent tool details disappear from debug view
no tool call history in logs panel
signals.review_reason: This is a feature request rather than a bug, but it documents a real pain point: users building complex agent applications cannot review tool call history for post-hoc debugging. Tool call details vanish after thinking ends, forcing users to reproduce issues. While not blocking, it materially degrades developer experience for agent workflows.

source_issues.title: [Feature] Persist Agent Tool Call Details in Logs and Debug Dialog
source_issues.evidence: Agent tool call details (parameters, responses, execution status) disappear from the Logs panel after thinking completes. Users must reproduce the issue to see tool call details again. Significantly reduces debugging efficiency for complex agent workflows.

signals.topic: OSS REST server rejects or ignores client-advertised fields (metadata-only updates, timestamp) causing 422 errors
signals.summary: The Python MemoryClient advertises and accepts metadata-only updates and timestamp fields, but the OSS REST server defines `MemoryUpdate.text` as required, returning 422 for both cases. Additionally, when `text + timestamp` are both sent, the server silently drops the timestamp. Users following the client's own API contract hit immediate failures.
aliases: Client-server API contract mismatch: metadata and timestamp fields
MemoryClient.update() fields rejected by OSS REST server
Client advertises timestamp support but server ignores/drops it
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues all describing the same root cause: client-server API contract mismatch. Users who follow the documented Python client API hit immediate 422 failures or 404 errors when pointing the client at the OSS REST server. This is not a test-only issue — it breaks the primary workflow of self-hosted mem0 deployments.

source_issues.title: Metadata-only memory updates are accepted by the client but rejected by the OSS REST server
source_issues.evidence: Client accepts `update(memory_id, metadata={...})` as valid per its own validation. Server returns 422 because `text` is required in `MemoryUpdate` Pydantic model.

source_issues.title: Client `update(..., timestamp=...)` is documented as supported but the REST server rejects or drops it
source_issues.evidence: Client accepts `timestamp` in update calls and sends it to server. Server returns 422 for timestamp-only updates (text required) and silently drops timestamp in combined updates.

source_issues.title: Custom `host` in the Python client cannot talk to the documented OSS REST server
source_issues.evidence: Python client hardcodes `/v1/...` paths for all endpoints. OSS REST server exposes only bare paths (`/memories`, `/search`, etc.). Self-hosted users following integration docs get immediate 404 on `GET /v1/ping/` during client init, and all subsequent operations target non-existent routes.

signals.topic: Ollama/OpenRouter integration failures: wrong endpoints, URL ignored, and repeated memory parsing errors
signals.summary: Three separate issues reveal systematic failures when using non-OpenAI LLM backends: (1) TypeScript SDK LLM config manager ignores custom `url` field and routes to `api.openai.com`, (2) mem0 uses `/v1/embeddings` instead of Ollama's `/api/embeddings` causing immediate network failure, (3) OpenRouter GPT-4o-mini causes repeated 'Failed to parse memory actions/facts from LLM response' errors with memories silently skipped. Together these represent complete functional failure of memory capture for self-hosted/local LLM users.
aliases: TypeScript SDK ignores custom LLM URL and routes to api.openai.com
Ollama embedder uses wrong /v1/embeddings endpoint instead of /api/embeddings
OpenRouter causes repeated memory extraction parsing failures
signals.review_reason: Three issues with shared root cause: systematic mishandling of non-OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoints. Self-hosted users relying on Ollama or OpenRouter get either immediate crashes (wrong endpoints, URL ignored) or repeated silent failures (parsing errors skipping memories). This blocks the primary use case of mem0 for the significant population of self-hosted/local LLM users.

source_issues.title: LLM config manager ignores url field — Ollama/custom LLM providers connect to api.openai.com
source_issues.evidence: TypeScript `ConfigManager.mergeConfig()` for LLM skips `userConf.url` in the fallback chain, falling back to `defaultConf.baseURL` of `https://api.openai.com/v1`. Users configuring Ollama with a custom URL see requests go to OpenAI instead, resulting in TypeError: fetch failed or 404.

source_issues.title: mem0 plugin fails with TypeError: fetch failed when using Ollama — wrong embeddings endpoint (/v1/embeddings)
source_issues.evidence: mem0 plugin attempts to call `POST /v1/embeddings` against Ollama, which only exposes `/api/embeddings`. Every embedding lookup fails with `TypeError: fetch failed`. Plugin is completely non-functional for Ollama embedder users.

source_issues.title: openclaw-mem0 / mem0ai OSS: Failed to parse memory actions from LLM response when using OpenRouter (gpt-4o-mini)
source_issues.evidence: User reports repeated `Failed to parse memory actions from LLM response` and `Failed to parse facts from LLM response` errors when using OpenRouter GPT-4o-mini. Memories are silently skipped, actions become empty. This happens repeatedly, not intermittently. Issue persists even after switching to stronger models.

signals.topic: Memory pipeline silently swallows LLM errors, returning empty results with no error signal
signals.summary: The `_add_to_vector_store` method wraps LLM response parsing in a bare `except Exception` that silently swallows KeyError/TypeError when the model omits required keys or returns unexpected shapes. Memory.add() then returns `{"results": []}` with no indication of failure, making transient LLM glitches indistinguishable from genuinely empty inputs. Observed downstream causing real debugging difficulty for users building on top of mem0.
aliases: Memory.add returns empty results with no error on parsing failures
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point because the memory pipeline silently fails with no error signal — users receive empty `{"results": []}` and cannot distinguish 'no facts to store' from 'pipeline actually broke.' The aldeia-box downstream issue provides concrete user impact evidence showing a real deployment was misled by this silent failure.

source_issues.title: _add_to_vector_store catches Exception, silently turning LLM errors into empty fact lists
source_issues.evidence: Bare `except Exception` in `_add_to_vector_store` at `mem0/memory/main.py:531` silently sets `new_retrieved_facts=[]` on any parsing error. `Memory.add` returns `{"results": []}` with no error. Downstream user at Aldeia-IT/aldeia-box#148 experienced this as a silent memory pipeline failure that took significant debugging to identify.

signals.topic: OpenClaw gateway enters infinite startup failure loop when anonymousTelemetryId is not declared in plugin schema
signals.summary: After OpenClaw gateway first run, `anonymousTelemetryId` is persisted to `openclaw.json` but is not declared in the plugin's JSON Schema (`additionalProperties: false`) nor the runtime `ALLOWED_KEYS` allowlist. On every restart, gateway config validation rejects the field, gateway fails to start, plugin re-writes the field on next registration — creating a permanent unresolvable loop that blocks the entire OpenClaw startup.
aliases: openclaw-mem0 infinite restart loop due to undeclared config field
Gateway startup crashes on restart due to missing schema declaration
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point because it creates a complete startup block: the OpenClaw gateway cannot start at all after the first run, and the user cannot resolve this without patching the plugin schema. The infinite loop means the entire OpenClaw system is unusable for affected users. The crash is in the main process initialization, making it a primary workflow blocker.

source_issues.title: [Bug][OpenClaw] anonymousTelemetryId not declared in configSchema/ALLOWED_KEYS causes infinite startup failure loop
source_issues.evidence: Plugin writes `anonymousTelemetryId` to `openclaw.json` on first run. On restart, JSON Schema validation fails (`must NOT have additional properties`) and runtime allowlist rejects the field. Even manually removing the field causes the plugin to re-write it, creating a permanent unresolvable startup failure loop.

signals.topic: Memory.add() crashes with AttributeError when vision is disabled and message content is a list
signals.summary: When `enable_vision=False` (the default), `Memory.add()` calls `parse_vision_messages()` without passing an LLM instance. However, the list-typed and `image_url`-dict content branches unconditionally call `llm.generate_response()` on a None value, causing `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'generate_response'`. This is a crash in the primary `Memory.add()` entry point, triggered by standard multimodal message formats produced by OpenAI SDK, LangChain, and other mainstream tools.
aliases: Memory.add crashes on list-typed message content with vision disabled
parse_vision_messages crashes with AttributeError on standard multimodal messages
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point because `Memory.add()` is the primary entry point for the core SDK and it crashes on standard, widely-used message formats from mainstream frameworks. The crash occurs in the default configuration, meaning any user passing multimodal-format messages (a very common pattern with modern LLM integrations) encounters an immediate unhandled exception. The traceback shows a clear `AttributeError` in production code, not a handled error.

source_issues.title: fix: AttributeError crash in Memory.add() when message content is a list and vision is disabled
source_issues.evidence: Core `Memory.add()` entry point crashes with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'generate_response'` when processing standard multimodal message format (`[{"type": "text", "text": "..."}]`), which is the default output format of OpenAI SDK, LangChain, and other major frameworks. Default `enable_vision=False` path does not pass an LLM to `parse_vision_messages()`, causing unconditional None dereference.

signals.topic: AG-UI: Python state and forwardedProps not passed to AgentSession, breaking ContextProvider and agent context
signals.summary: The Python AG-UI implementation fails to pass both session state and forwardedProps to AgentSession. forwardedProps is parsed but silently dropped; state is not forwarded at all. This prevents ContextProvider from receiving agent_id, user_id, tenant_id and blocks integration with HistoryProvider and other context-dependent features.

signals.review_reason: Two separate issues with the same root cause: AG-UI integration in Python does not bridge state and forwardedProps to the agent session. This breaks ContextProvider, HistoryProvider, and any agent or tool that needs identity or tenant context—a core integration path for AG-UI users.

signals.topic: Python: Message ID collision during session compaction corrupts message history
signals.summary: The _ensure_message_ids function assigns sequential msg_N IDs based on list index, and when annotate_message_groups calls it on slices of the message list, incremental compaction runs collide with already-assigned IDs, corrupting history and breaking downstream logic.
signals.review_reason: Corrupts the message history by assigning duplicate IDs during session compaction. This breaks any logic relying on message identity (e.g., reference tracking, deduplication) and is a silent data corruption issue in a core workflow path.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Colliding Ids are assigned to message history creating issues when using compaction
source_issues.evidence: _ensure_message_ids(messages) in agent_framework/_compaction.py fills each missing Message.message_id with f'msg_{index}' where index is position in the list. annotate_message_groups calls it on a slice of the full list, so successive incremental calls collide with ids already assigned.

signals.topic: Python: OTel _finalize_stream triggers result hooks on streaming errors, causing incorrect after_run provider invocations
signals.summary: AgentTelemetryLayer registers _finalize_stream as a cleanup hook that runs on both normal and error completions. Since get_final_response() always runs result hooks, after_run context providers fire even when the stream errored, causing incorrect side effects.
aliases: OTel cleanup hook fires on error
after_run providers fire on stream error
signals.review_reason: Telemetry/observability bug that causes after_run context providers to fire on streaming errors, leading to incorrect side effects. While not a direct crash, it pollutes monitoring data and can cause incorrect business logic to execute based on a failed response.

source_issues.title: Python: OTel _finalize_stream triggers result hooks on streaming error, causing after_run providers to fire incorrectly
source_issues.evidence: AgentTelemetryLayer._trace_agent_invocation registers _finalize_stream as a cleanup hook on the ResponseStream. Cleanup hooks run on both normal completion and streaming errors. get_final_response() always runs result hooks, causing after_run context providers to fire even when the stream errored.

signals.topic: MagenticOneGroupChat loses conversation context after human-in-the-loop handoff to user
signals.summary: When using HandoffTermination to hand off to a user in MagenticOneGroupChat, the conversation context is lost after user input. The same setup works correctly with RoundRobinGroupChat. Users report that after a handoff, subsequent user input is treated as a completely new conversation instead of continuing the existing one, breaking core HiTL workflow expectations.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed functional regression in MagenticOneGroupChat vs RoundRobinGroupChat. The user provided full reproducible code demonstrating that the same HiTL handoff pattern works with RoundRobinGroupChat but breaks with MagenticOneGroupChat. Context loss after user handoff is a main-flow blocker for HiTL workflows, which is a documented AutoGen use case. The issue has been recently active with maintainer engagement, indicating it is a legitimate unresolved bug.

signals.topic: RoundRobinGroupChat raises opaque internal errors instead of clear validation messages for invalid participants

This makes debugging realistic user mistakes unnecessarily difficult.
signals.review_reason: While count=1, this qualifies as a user pain point because the author demonstrates multiple realistic invalid-input scenarios that all produce opaque internal errors. The experience degradation is concrete: users encountering these mistakes must parse raw Python tracebacks instead of getting an actionable validation message. This is a straightforward quality-of-life fix with clear user impact, though it is not a main-flow blocker.

signals.topic: /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests with no error or retry

signals.review_reason: Memory leak confirmed by flame graph; accumulates indefinitely in long-running processes. Blocks production use of structured outputs with image data. Reproduction steps provided. Single repo but clear main-flow blocking impact on memory-constrained environments.

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Memory leak confirmed via flame graph. Pydantic models left behind after parsing large base64 images. Affects AsyncResponses.parse() API with Pydantic models.

signals.topic: AsyncCompletions.parse() memory leak with dynamically created Pydantic models
signals.summary: Using AsyncCompletions.parse() with Pydantic models created via create_model causes memory to grow unboundedly. No plateau observed — parsers built on these models are not garbage collected across repeated calls.
signals.review_reason: Memory leak confirmed via memory_profiler over 200 calls with no plateau. Blocks production use of structured outputs in the beta Chat Completions parse path. Reproduction code and workaround provided. Main-flow blocking for any long-running process.

source_issues.title: Possible memory leak in `AsyncCompletions.parse()`
source_issues.evidence: Memory profiler shows unbounded growth over 200 calls. Workaround exists (use non-parse API with type_to_response_format_param), but the parse() path leaks. No plateau observed in memory usage.

signals.topic: PydanticUserError in multiprocess forkserver workers with defer_build=True
signals.summary: With openai SDK and pydantic 2.12+, deserializing chat completion responses in multiprocess forkserver workers raises PydanticUserError due to deferred pydantic model rebuild failing in forked processes. Causes ~0.6%% failure rate with defer_build=true and ~9.5%% without, in production systems processing millions of requests.
signals.review_reason: High failure rates (0.6-9.5%%) in a large-scale production multiprocess deployment. Root cause traced to pydantic model rebuild in forked processes. While single-repo, the user impact is significant (millions of requests, ~700 workers). P1 due to count=1 (single repo) but strong user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: PydanticUserError with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12 in multiprocess forkserver workers
source_issues.evidence: ~0.6%% error rate with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true, ~9.5%% without. Affects production with ~700 forkserver workers processing millions of requests. Root cause: _parent_namespace_depth=5 in model_rebuild fails in forked processes.

signals.topic: Server-side compaction not emitted on Responses API tool-call-only turns, causing context_length_exceeded
signals.summary: In the Responses API, server-side compaction is not emitted when a turn produces only function_call output. Context continues growing across consecutive tool-call turns, eventually hitting context_length_exceeded before any compaction appears. Only emits compaction once the model finally returns an assistant message.
aliases: compaction not emitted tool calls Responses API
signals.review_reason: Real main-flow blocking issue in agentic tool-use loops. Server-side compaction feature is fundamentally broken for tool-call-only turns, leading to context accumulation and eventual context_length_exceeded errors. Clear reproduction with token count evidence.

source_issues.title: Bug: server-side compaction is not emitted on Responses tool-call-only turns
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows input_tokens growing from 5084 to 5119 to 5154 across consecutive function_call-only turns, with compaction only appearing once a message is returned. Agent loops can hit context_length_exceeded before compaction is ever emitted.

signals.topic: Image token cost documentation ambiguous across models, causing unexpected billing in production
signals.summary: Documentation mixes BASE/TILE and PATCH*MULTIPLIER image cost systems across different model families without clearly stating which model each applies to. Developers cannot accurately predict costs, leading to unexpected billing behavior in production.
signals.review_reason: Direct cost/billing impact — developers cannot predict image token costs, leading to unexpected billing. While a documentation issue rather than a code bug, the business impact (unpredictable costs) qualifies as a user pain point. P2 due to count=1 and documentation-only scope.

source_issues.title: Image token cost documentation is ambiguous across models (BASE/TILE vs PATCH*MULTIPLIER)
source_issues.evidence: Statement 'detail: low lets the model process with ~85 tokens' is true for GPT-4o-class but false for 4o-mini and GPT-5-mini which follow different rules. Documentation does not explicitly state model scope for each cost system, causing cost unpredictability in production.

signals.topic: ACP inter-node pairing fails with 'unknown requestId' preventing device approval
signals.summary: When attempting to connect two OpenClaw instances via ACP (e.g., Mac client to Azure VM server), the pairing request shows as pending but device approval fails with 'GatewayClientRequestError: unknown requestId', blocking the ACP inter-node connection workflow.
aliases: devices approve all fails with unknown requestId
signals.review_reason: ACP device pairing is a core workflow that is actively broken. The `openclaw devices approve all` command throws an unhandled GatewayClientRequestError and fails to approve the pending ACP device, preventing inter-node ACP connections. This blocks the main use case of connecting remote OpenClaw agents. Evidence is concrete with full error stack traces and reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: Connect to another OpenClaw via ACP issue
source_issues.evidence: User sets up ACP connection between Mac (client) and Azure VM (server), runs `openclaw devices list` showing pending ACP device with requestId, but `openclaw devices approve all` fails with 'GatewayClientRequestError: unknown requestId'. Workaround via `openclaw.json` basePath config partially helps pairing handshake but approval still fails.

signals.topic: acpx claude exec fails with 'Invalid permissions.defaultMode: auto' blocking ACP runtime execution
signals.summary: Running `acpx claude exec` or spawning via `sessions_spawn` with `runtime: 'acp'` immediately fails because the ACP SDK sends `permissions.defaultMode: 'auto'` which Claude ACP runtime rejects as invalid. Users must fall back to direct CLI, bypassing acpx entirely.
aliases: acpx claude exec permissions.defaultMode auto invalid
signals.review_reason: The `acpx claude exec` command, a primary entry point for running Claude via ACP, is completely broken due to an unsupported permissions.defaultMode value. The error occurs at session initialization, making the entire ACP runtime unusable for the claude runtime. Users are forced to bypass acpx entirely as a workaround, indicating a critical functional block.

source_issues.title: claude exec fails with 'Invalid permissions.defaultMode: auto' - session/new sends unsupported defaultMode
source_issues.evidence: `acpx claude exec` fails immediately with 'Internal error: Invalid permissions.defaultMode: auto'. The `session/new` JSON-RPC request sends an unsupported value that claude-agent-acp rejects. Users must use direct `claude --print --permission-mode bypassPermissions` as workaround, fully bypassing acpx.

signals.topic: Persistent session resumption fails because sessionDir is always null in session index
signals.summary: When creating a persistent session with `-s <name>`, the session index JSON stores `sessionDir: null`, causing `prompt` to fail with 'No acpx session found' even though `status` and `sessions` commands show the session exists. This breaks the core persistent session workflow.
aliases: prompt fails no acpx session found with sessionDir null
signals.review_reason: Persistent sessions are a core advertised feature of acpx. The session index is written with `sessionDir: null`, making the `prompt` command completely unusable for resuming sessions, even though the session exists in the index. This is a clear functional regression that breaks the main value proposition of named persistent sessions. Steps to reproduce are exact and root cause is confirmed.

source_issues.title: Persistent sessions: sessionDir is null, prompt cannot find session
source_issues.evidence: User creates a named persistent session with `acpx gemini -s test_session exec 'hello'`, then `status` and `sessions` correctly list it, but `prompt` fails with 'No acpx session found (searched up to /home/user/workspace)'. The root cause is `sessionDir: null` in the session index JSON at `~/.acpx/sessions/<uuid>.json`, which breaks the session directory resolution path for `prompt`.

signals.topic: Approval gate resume token invalid across separate tool calls
signals.summary: When a workflow pauses for approval and returns a resume token, using that token in a subsequent tool call fails with 'Invalid token' or 'Invalid pipeline resume state', blocking the core approval-gate workflow pattern.
aliases: resume token invalid across tool calls
signals.review_reason: This is a concrete, reproducible bug that blocks the core approval-gate workflow pattern. The resume token mechanism is the primary way users interact with approval gates in Lobster, yet it fails across tool call boundaries. The hypothesis points to in-memory storage of resume state — the fix is a clear persistence requirement. A user-level workaround exists but forces users to abandon the approval gate primitive entirely, which is a significant capability regression.

source_issues.title: lobster resume: token invalid across tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Repro: pipeline with approval gate returns needs_approval + resumeToken; calling lobster resume --token <token> in the next tool call fails with 'Invalid token' (inline mode) or 'Invalid pipeline resume state' (file mode). Workaround: avoid approval gates entirely.

signals.topic: Windows: ollama launch openclaw creates duplicate gateway process when Scheduled Task is already running, causing port conflict, EPERM errors, and gateway instability
signals.summary: When OpenClaw Gateway runs as a Windows Scheduled Task (Session 0), `ollama launch openclaw` fails to detect it and spawns a second node.exe process binding the same port 18789, leading to mDNS name conflicts, RPC probe failures, EPERM file-write errors on pending.json, handshake timeouts, and gateway crashes (1006).
aliases: ollama launch creates double gateway on Windows
signals.review_reason: This is a real user-impacting bug on Windows where the gateway detection logic fails due to Session 0 process isolation, causing duplicate processes, port conflicts (EPERM errors on shared files), and gateway instability. Severity is P1 (not P0) because count=1 and it is single-repo, but user impact is clear and concrete with multiple failure symptoms documented.

source_issues.title: [Windows] ollama launch openclaw starts duplicate gateway when Scheduled Task is already running
source_issues.evidence: User reports: two LISTENING entries on port 18789 after `ollama launch openclaw`; mDNS name conflict renamed to `DESKTOP-xxx (OpenClaw) (2)`; `RPC probe: failed`; `EPERM` errors writing `~/.openclaw/devices/pending.json`; mass `handshake timeout` and `gateway closed (1006)` errors; root cause identified as Session 0 isolation preventing cross-session process enumeration.

signals.topic: Windows Tray App does not auto-reconnect after Gateway restart, leaving node permanently disconnected until manual toggle
signals.summary: After an OpenClaw Gateway restart, the Windows Tray App (Node Mode) remains in a permanently disconnected state and never attempts reconnection, unlike the CLI node which has automatic retry logic. Users must manually toggle Node Mode off and on to recover.
aliases: Tray App node disconnected after gateway restart
Node Mode fails to reconnect after gateway restart
signals.review_reason: Clear user-facing bug: the Tray App node mode becomes permanently unusable after any gateway restart, with no automatic recovery mechanism. This is a key functional breakdown for users relying on the Tray App as their node interface. The contrast with the CLI node (which reconnects automatically) makes the missing behavior clearly a defect, not an intended design.

source_issues.title: Windows Tray App does not auto-reconnect after Gateway restart
source_issues.evidence: User reports: after Gateway restart, Tray App shows `[INFO] Node status changed: Disconnected` and stays disconnected indefinitely with no reconnection attempts logged. CLI node (`openclaw node run`) correctly reconnects with `Node reconnecting in 1000ms (attempt 1)` but Tray App lacks this logic. Requires manual workaround: toggle Node Mode off → wait 2-3s → toggle on. Affects remote gateway over WSS (Nginx TLS reverse proxy) and Session 0 isolation scenarios.

Any user trying to use Comfy for image/video/music generation is blocked.
signals.review_reason: Key bundled feature (Comfy image/video/music generation) is completely inaccessible to all users due to broken schema validation. Config rejected at load time — no workaround without patching compiled JS.

signals.topic: Dashboard WebSocket fails to reconnect after gateway restart — token_mismatch then rate_limited lockout

signals.review_reason: Gateway restart is a routine operational action but causes complete dashboard lockout requiring manual user intervention. Token refresh mechanism is missing, creating unnecessary downtime for all users who restart their gateway.

source_issues.title: Dashboard WebSocket disconnects with token_mismatch after gateway restart

signals.review_reason: Core group chat functionality is completely broken — messages are silently swallowed with no error feedback to user. This is a regression of previously fixed issues, indicating a code path was re-broken. Users have no indication their messages were received.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Group natural-language messages silently dropped in 2026.4.11 (regression of #29637/#30591)

signals.topic: System prompt does not respect OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR — agent operates on wrong workspace path

signals.review_reason: For headless/cloud deployments that rely on remote workspace volumes, the agent operates on the wrong filesystem path. This means all file and memory operations fail silently against the intended workspace, directly undermining the core deployment model for cloud users.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: System Prompt doesn't respect OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR
source_issues.evidence: On EC2/ECS with OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR set to a remote volume path, system prompt shows local default path. Agent operations miss all content on the EFS volume. Workaround requires agent-level runtime detection.
