aliases: Git repo working tree dir None causes TypeError
Aider crashes on startup with TypeError in pathlib
signals.review_reason: TypeError 导致启动时即崩溃属于主流程阻断，用户完全无法使用 Aider。未捕获异常直接导致 main() 退出，进程非正常终止，构成关键功能不可用。

source_issues.title: Uncaught TypeError in pathlib.py line 373
source_issues.evidence: 用户启动 Aider 时 GitRepo 初始化失败，working_tree_dir 返回 None 导致 pathlib.Path 抛出 TypeError，Aider 无法运行。

signals.topic: "Don't ask again" 选项设置不生效，用户每次启动都重复收到相同提示
signals.summary: 用户选择 'D' (Don't ask again) 选项后，相同问题在每次 Aider 启动时仍然重复出现，设置未持久化保存。
aliases: prompt 'Don't ask again' option not persisting across sessions
user preferences not saved between sessions
signals.review_reason: "Don't ask again" 是用户用于减少重复交互的核心选项，其不生效导致用户在每次启动时都被重复提示，构成反复体验下降，但非主流程阻断。

source_issues.title: "Don't ask again" does not work
source_issues.evidence: 用户对未知模型警告选择 'D' (Don't ask again)，下次启动 Aider 仍出现相同提示，确认设置未持久化。

signals.topic: Web UI crashes with circular JSON error when using LLM providers (Bedrock/Anthropic) as llm-rubric judge
signals.summary: When using any LLM provider (AWS Bedrock or Anthropic) as the judge for llm-rubric assertions via defaultTest.options.provider, running an eval from the web UI throws a 'Converting circular structure to JSON' error and the eval never executes. The same configuration works correctly from CLI.
aliases: circular JSON serialization error in UI
UI eval fails with LLM judge provider
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断性 bug：Web UI 场景下 eval 完全无法执行，用户切换到 UI 模式后所有基于 llm-rubric 的评估均失败。虽然 CLI 可以绕过，但 UI 是 promptfoo 的核心使用界面，该阻断直接影响用户正常工作流。

source_issues.title: Converting circular structure to JSON when using Bedrock provider as llm-rubric judge in UI
source_issues.evidence: Bug prevents eval from executing in the web UI. Error: 'TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON' for both Bedrock and Anthropic SDK clients when serialized for web worker. Works in CLI but not in UI.

signals.topic: promptfoo redteam discover fails with 'Unknown task: target-purpose-discovery' error
signals.summary: The `promptfoo redteam discover` command makes a POST request to the promptfoo.app API with task name 'target-purpose-discovery' which returns HTTP 400, while `promptfoo redteam generate` with the same credentials works correctly. The discover feature is completely non-functional.
aliases: redteam discover broken on promptfoo.app API
signals.review_reason: 关键功能完全不可用：redteam discover 是 redteam 模块的核心发现功能，该命令对所有用户均返回 400 错误，完全无法使用。虽然是单仓库问题，但功能完全阻断，count=1 仍值得标记为 P1。

source_issues.title: `promptfoo redteam discover` fails with `Unknown task: target-purpose-discovery`
source_issues.evidence: redteam discover 100% broken: all requests return HTTP 400 with error 'Unknown task: target-purpose-discovery'. Same endpoint + same credentials work for redteam generate (HTTP 200). Only the 'target-purpose-discovery' task name triggers the failure.

signals.topic: handleGEval silently fails with NaN score and empty reason when value is an empty array
signals.summary: When g-eval assertion receives an empty array as value, the score computation results in NaN (0/0), the pass/fail silently defaults to false, and the reason field is empty — giving users zero actionable feedback.
aliases: geval silent false-fail no error message
signals.review_reason: 静默失败（silent false-fail）：用户收到 FAIL 结果但无任何可操作的错误信息（score 为 NaN，reason 为空），完全无法定位根因。eval 流程看似正常但实际判断错误，属于关键功能体验严重下降。

source_issues.title: bug: handleGEval returns NaN score and silent false-fail when value is an empty array
source_issues.evidence: Empty array input causes scoresSum/scores.length = 0/0 = NaN. Assertion reports FAIL with score: NaN and reason: '' (empty string). No error message is shown to user, making debugging impossible.

signals.topic: rouge assertion returns factually incorrect reason messages when inverse: true
signals.summary: When rouge assertion has inverse: true, the pass/fail logic is correct but the human-readable reason field says the opposite of what happened — claiming score is >= threshold when it actually isn't, and vice versa. Other similar assertions (bleu, gleu) handle this correctly.
signals.review_reason: 误导性反馈：虽然 rouge 的通过/失败逻辑本身正确，但 reason 字段给出与实际结果相反的描述，用户基于错误信息做判断，影响 eval 结果的可信度。bleu/gleu 已正确处理，rouge 是已知的不一致实现。

source_issues.title: Bug: rouge assertion returns incorrect reason message when inverse: true
source_issues.evidence: With inverse:true and score=0.3, threshold=0.8, pass=true (correct) but reason says 'is greater than or equal to threshold' (factually wrong, 0.3 < 0.8). The pass/fail logic is correct but reason text is inverted.

signals.topic: vLLM LLM integration breaks completely on every .complete() call due to removed 'best_of' parameter in vLLM >= 0.19.0
signals.summary: vLLM LLM integration unconditionally passes 'best_of' to SamplingParams, which was removed in vLLM 0.19.0. Every .complete() call raises TypeError, making the integration unusable with recent vLLM versions.
signals.review_reason: Every .complete() call raises TypeError, making the vLLM LLM integration completely unusable with recent vLLM versions. This is a main flow failure for any user relying on vLLM as an LLM backend. The issue is deterministic, reproducible, and has no non-patching workaround.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: llama-index-llms-vllm: best_of removed from vLLM SamplingParams causes TypeError on .complete()
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Unexpected keyword argument 'best_of' raised on every Vllm.complete() call with vLLM >= 0.19.0. Integration completely unusable — no workaround without patching.

signals.topic: PDFReader Path() casting breaks S3 file loading, making SimpleDirectoryReader with S3 fs unusable for PDFs
signals.summary: PDFReader unconditionally converts file paths to Path objects, converting S3 URIs to WindowsPath on Windows environments. S3FileSystem rejects these paths, causing every S3-based PDF load to fail silently with ValueError.
signals.review_reason: PDF loading from S3 is completely blocked — every PDF file fails to load when using S3FileSystem with SimpleDirectoryReader. This breaks the primary use case for S3-based PDF ingestion workflows and has been open since August 2024 with no resolution.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: impossible to use PDFReader with an S3 file because of Path() casting
source_issues.evidence: ValueError: 'Attempt to open non key-like path' when using SimpleDirectoryReader with S3FileSystem to load PDFs. PDFReader converts S3 paths to Path objects, which S3FileSystem cannot handle. All PDF files from S3 fail to load.

signals.topic: Cross-provider agent workflows fail with OpenAI 400 BadRequestError because tool_kwargs are not JSON-serialized
signals.summary: When an agent using Anthropic LLM hands off to an OpenAI LLM agent, the OpenAI API returns 400 because tool_kwargs (a Python dict) is passed directly as function.arguments instead of a JSON string.
signals.review_reason: Cross-provider agent workflows are completely blocked — the handoff from an Anthropic LLM orchestrator to an OpenAI sub-agent fails with a 400 API error on every tool call. This defeats the entire purpose of the AgentWorkflow multi-provider feature. The fix already exists in the Responses API path but was not applied to the Chat Completions API path.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: to_openai_message_dict doesn't JSON-serialize ToolCallBlock.tool_kwargs and breaks cross-provider agent workflows
source_issues.evidence: OpenAI API returns 400 BadRequestError: 'Invalid type for messages[3].tool_calls[0].function.arguments: expected a string, but got an object'. Occurs when Anthropic LLM orchestrator hands off to OpenAI sub-agent in AgentWorkflow. Deterministic and blocks the core multi-agent orchestration feature.

signals.topic: FunctionAgent returns empty response on second and subsequent calls despite shared Context, breaking conversational agent workflows
signals.summary: When a FunctionAgent is called multiple times with the same Context object, the first response is correct but all subsequent responses are empty strings. The agent correctly receives context (e.g., user name) in the first turn but cannot access it in follow-up turns.
signals.review_reason: Conversational agent workflows are broken — follow-up turns return empty responses, making persistent-context agents unusable for any real conversational use case. This is a main flow failure for the FunctionAgent/Context pattern, despite the documentation showing it should work. Open since November 2025.

source_issues.title: [Question]: why the second reponse is empty?
source_issues.evidence: Second workflow.run() call returns empty string despite Context object being shared. Agent correctly answers 'Hi Laurie' in first turn but returns empty on 'what's my name?' in second turn. Documentation shows this should work but it does not.

signals.topic: ElasticsearchStore.query() silently ignores metadata_keyword_suffix on the synchronous path
signals.summary: The sync wrapper for ElasticsearchStore.query() does not forward metadata_keyword_suffix to the async implementation, causing custom metadata suffix filtering to silently use the default '.keyword' suffix instead.
signals.review_reason: Users relying on the standard synchronous retrieval path get silently incorrect behavior — their metadata filters use the wrong suffix, leading to failed or incorrect query results without any error message. This is a silent data correctness issue that is difficult to debug.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ElasticsearchStore.query() ignores metadata_keyword_suffix on the synchronous path
source_issues.evidence: metadata_keyword_suffix parameter is silently dropped when calling the sync query path. Users expecting custom metadata suffix filtering get incorrect default behavior with no error or warning. The async path works correctly.

signals.topic: vectorBackend config missing causes 8 controllers to fail on every startup
signals.summary: ControllerRegistry.initAgentDB() does not pass vectorBackend config to AgentDB, causing AgentDB to fall back to HNSWLib and returning null for the vectorBackend controller. This cascades to 7 other dependent controllers (mutationGuard, gnnService, attestationLog, semanticRouter, guardedVectorBackend, rvfOptimizer, graphAdapter), all marked as failed.
signals.review_reason: Blocking bug — 8 of 23 controllers fail on every startup due to missing vectorBackend config. Cascading failure affecting core functionality (mutationGuard, gnnService, attestationLog, semanticRouter, guardedVectorBackend, rvfOptimizer, graphAdapter). Single issue but clear root cause and wide impact across the controller system.

source_issues.title: Bug: ControllerRegistry.initAgentDB() does not pass vectorBackend config — AgentDB falls back to HNSWLib and vectorBackend controller always returns null
source_issues.evidence: 8 of 23 controllers fail on every startup. Cascading failure affecting 7 dependent controllers. ControllerRegistry reports Activated: 15 Failed: 8 instead of Activated: 23 Failed: 0. Core vector backend never activates.

signals.topic: Windows Codex: MCP stdio transport crashes after first memory tool call
signals.summary: On Windows, the MCP server starts successfully and responds to mcp_status, but the first memory_search or memory_store call causes the stdio transport to close. All subsequent MCP calls fail with 'Transport closed'.
aliases: Windows MCP transport dies on first memory call
stdio transport closes after memory tool call on Windows
signals.review_reason: Complete Windows blocker — MCP server becomes unusable after first memory tool call. mcp_status works but no other MCP operations do. Process-level crash likely below JS exception boundaries.

source_issues.title: Windows Codex: first memory MCP tool call closes stdio transport after successful startup
source_issues.evidence: On Windows, MCP server starts and responds to mcp_status but first memory_search/memory_store call causes 'Transport closed' error. All subsequent MCP calls fail. Likely sql.js WASM crash or unhandled promise rejection below JS exception boundaries.

signals.topic: init --skip-claude silently overwrites user's global CLAUDE.md causing permanent data loss
signals.summary: Running 'ruflo init --skip-claude --minimal' overwrites the user's global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (42 lines of workflow rules, project knowledge, session hooks) with a 4-line stub, with no backup created.
signals.review_reason: Critical data loss bug — user customization permanently destroyed with no backup. Flag name and documentation promise safety that is violated. Single issue but high severity.

source_issues.title: init --skip-claude overwrites ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md without backup
source_issues.evidence: User's global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (42 lines of workflow rules, project knowledge, session hooks) permanently destroyed and replaced with 4-line stub. No backup created. Documentation promises --skip-claude skips .claude/ directory creation but it modifies ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md anyway.

signals.topic: npm init fails completely due to Invalid Version in koa-router@14.0.0 dependency tree
signals.summary: 'npx @claude-flow/cli@latest init --wizard' fails immediately with 'npm error Invalid Version:' because koa-router@14.0.0 has a transitive dependency with an invalid semver string that npm v11 rejects during canDedupe.
aliases: npm install fails on init command
signals.review_reason: Complete blocker — users cannot run init at all due to invalid semver in transitive dependency. Affects all new users trying to set up the project.

source_issues.title: npm error: Invalid Version in koa-router@14.0.0 dependency tree (v3.5.78)
source_issues.evidence: 'npx @claude-flow/cli@latest init --wizard' fails immediately with 'npm error Invalid Version:' (empty version string). Root cause: koa-router@14.0.0 has a transitive dependency with invalid semver. npm v11's stricter validation rejects it during canDedupe.

signals.topic: MCP tools fail on Windows because process.cwd() resolves to System32
signals.summary: All MCP tool files use process.cwd() for storage paths (.claude-flow/swarm/, .claude-flow/agents/). On Windows, AI coding agents launch MCP server via npx which inherits C:\Windows\System32 as cwd — a read-only system directory. Every tool that writes state fails with EPERM.
aliases: all MCP tools fail on Windows due to cwd
signals.review_reason: Complete Windows failure — all MCP tool state persistence broken on Windows. process.cwd() in child process inherits System32. 16+ files affected.

source_issues.title: MCP tools use process.cwd() which resolves to System32 on Windows
source_issues.evidence: All MCP tool files use process.cwd() for storage paths (.claude-flow/swarm/, .claude-flow/agents/). On Windows, AI coding agents launch MCP server via npx which inherits C:\Windows\System32 as cwd — a read-only system directory. Every tool that writes state fails with 'EPERM: operation not permitted'. 16+ files affected across swarm-tools, agent-tools, coordination-tools.

signals.topic: Profile/persistent sessions lose active page state or crash, breaking multi-command workflows
signals.summary: When using --profile with persistent sessions, the first open succeeds but subsequent commands in the same session lose the active page (falling back to about:blank) or the daemon crashes silently. This makes persistent profile sessions unusable for any multi-step automation.
aliases: profile session crash after first command
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports (#1211, #1035) both show persistent session workflows failing after the first command — one loses the active page on macOS, one hangs entirely on Linux Server/NAS. Both represent complete workflow failure for the core use case of maintaining login state across commands. The Linux case additionally blocks headless server/CI environments entirely.

source_issues.title: `--profile` sessions lose the active page after the first command and fall back to `about:blank`
source_issues.evidence: On macOS with agent-browser 0.25.3, using --profile with a persistent directory: first open succeeds, second command (tab list/get url) reports about:blank. Daemon log shows WebSocket connection reset. Chrome itself has the correct page target but session reuse loses it.

source_issues.title: agent-browser open hangs on Linux Server/NAS - daemon fails to start (OpenClaw agent)
source_issues.evidence: On Linux Server/NAS (Ubuntu 24.04) with persistent profile, agent-browser open hangs indefinitely. No socket file ever created. Chrome process never starts. Error after 30s retries: 'Failed to connect: No such file or directory (os error 2)'. Blocks all headless server automation.

signals.topic: Chrome fails to launch on Linux containers/VMs/headless environments without --no-sandbox flag
signals.summary: On Linux environments with sandbox restrictions (containers, VMs, Ubuntu 23.10+, AppArmor), Chrome exits immediately with 'No usable sandbox' error before exposing a DevTools URL. The Agent Dashboard UI provides no way to pass --no-sandbox, making Chrome completely unusable in these environments.
aliases: Chrome exits with zygote sandbox error
no DevTools URL without sandbox flag
signals.review_reason: Two reports on Linux environments (Agent Dashboard and headless Server/NAS) where Chrome fails to start due to sandbox restrictions. This is a complete blocker for Docker containers, cloud VMs, CI runners, and hardened Linux hosts — increasingly common deployment targets. The lack of a configurable --no-sandbox flag in the UI forces users to use workarounds or switch tools.

source_issues.title: Add Chrome launch args support in Agent Dashboard UI (needed for `--no-sandbox` on some Linux/VM/container setups)
source_issues.evidence: Chrome exits immediately on Linux containers/VMs/Ubuntu 23.10+ with 'FATAL: content/browser/zygote_host/zygote_host_impl_linux.cc:128] No usable sandbox!'. No session is created. Agent Dashboard UI has no way to pass --no-sandbox or other launch flags.

source_issues.title: agent-browser open hangs on Linux Server/NAS - daemon fails to start (OpenClaw agent)
source_issues.evidence: On Linux Server/NAS environment, daemon never starts, Chrome never launches. Hypothesis: missing display/wayland environment variables or Chrome needing --no-sandbox but daemon not passing it.

signals.topic: CDP session isolation missing: cookies and storage leak between sessions on the same domain
signals.summary: Multiple agents/sessions connected to the same Chrome instance share the default BrowserContext, causing cookies and localStorage to collide. Two agents logging into the same domain with different credentials will overwrite each other's session. The --session flag provides tab isolation but not CDP-level storage isolation.
signals.review_reason: Two reports spanning a year (#86 from Jan, #1068 from Mar) confirm that sessions share browser state, causing credential collision. This is a fundamental correctness issue for multi-agent setups working on the same domain. It silently corrupts session state — agents may believe they're logged in as one user while actually using another's credentials.

source_issues.title: [Feature Request] CDP BrowserContext support for cookie-isolated parallel sessions
source_issues.evidence: When multiple agents use --auto-connect or connect to the same Chrome, all share the default BrowserContext. Cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage leak between sessions. Two agents on the same domain with different credentials experience session overwrite. The root cause is that --session only provides tab-namespace isolation, not CDP Target.createBrowserContext isolation.

source_issues.title: Support for Multi Session
source_issues.evidence: Two terminal panes using agent-browser skill simultaneously had their browser content intercept each other, suggesting shared browser instance. Content from one session appeared in the other.

signals.topic: Chrome crashes after ~7–9 seconds idle due to v0.24.1 PR_SET_PDEATHSIG regression
signals.summary: v0.24.1 introduced PR_SET_PDEATHSIG in Chrome's pre_exec hook. Because tokio's multi-threaded runtime recycles worker threads after idle, Chrome gets SIGKILL by the kernel even though the daemon is still alive. This breaks all workflows with >7s gaps between commands.
aliases: Chrome auto-restarts with about:blank after idle
signals.review_reason: This is a critical regression: it silently kills Chrome after idle on every single page, breaks download workflows completely, and blocks any automation with >7s gaps. While count=1, the per-incident impact is catastrophic and universal — every user who upgraded to v0.24.1 is affected on every automation run. The reporter provided a validated patch.

source_issues.title: fix: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG kills Chrome in tokio multi-threaded runtime (v0.24.1 regression)
source_issues.evidence: All pages navigate to about:blank after ~7-9 seconds idle on every site in both headless and headed mode. Downloads fail (first works, second fails). Live preview streaming shows resolution changes. Any automation with >7s between commands fails. Regression from v0.24.1, works in v0.24.0.

signals.topic: iOS provider doesn't expose mounted page selectors, blocking iOS Safari automation
signals.summary: When using the iOS provider to open local dev routes, the mounted page's DOM (e.g. the actual editor HTML) is never exposed — only the Next.js shell/scaffold is visible. Selector-based actions (click, type, eval) fail with element-not-found even though a human can see the real page in Safari.
aliases: iOS Safari mounted page selectors missing
signals.review_reason: This blocks the entire iOS Safari testing workflow. The agent cannot interact with mounted DOM content even though a human can see and interact with the same page via real Safari. This creates a fundamental parity gap between human-driven and agent-driven iOS testing. Only affects iOS provider but the impact is total for that provider.

source_issues.title: iOS provider opens local Next dev route but never exposes mounted page selectors
source_issues.evidence: iOS provider reports the correct URL but commands like click #placeholder-ime, type, eval return element-not-found/null. The same route works fine with direct Appium+XCUITest Safari on the same machine. Creates an agent-native parity gap for iOS Safari testing.

signals.topic: streamText deny approval crashes with 'Missing required parameter: input[N].output'
signals.summary: When user denies a tool call via addToolApprovalResponse({ approved: false }), the next step crashes with 'Missing required parameter: input[N].output' — approval flow is completely broken
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：approval deny流程是streamText的核心安全机制，用户点击拒绝后SDK直接崩溃，next POST请求直接失败。主流程完全不可用，影响所有使用needsApproval的用户。提供了完整curl复现和根因分析。

source_issues.title: streamText: deny approval crashes with 'Missing required parameter: input[N].output'
source_issues.evidence: User denied tool call via addToolApprovalResponse({ approved: false }) → SDK emits 'tool-output-denied' correctly → then crashes on next model call with 'Missing required parameter: input[N].output'. Both code patterns (convertToModelMessages + streamText, and raw messages) fail identically. Root cause traced to convertToLanguageModelPrompt filtering out non-provider-executed tool-approval-response parts from the tool message.

signals.topic: embed/embedMany crashes when used with EmbeddingModelV2 providers — 'warnings' is undefined
signals.summary: embed() and embedMany() crash at runtime with EmbeddingModelV2 providers because doEmbed does not return warnings property, causing TypeError in logWarnings and spread operator failure
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：embed/embedMany是SDK的核心embedding能力，使用EmbeddingModelV2协议的所有provider都会触发此crash（已确认google-vertex受影响）。运行时TypeError直接导致应用崩溃，是明确的用户影响阻断。

source_issues.title: embed/embedMany crash: 'warnings' is undefined from EmbeddingModelV2 providers
source_issues.evidence: embed() crashes at logWarnings with 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)'. embedMany() crashes with 'TypeError: result.warnings is not iterable' at spread operator. Confirmed with @ai-sdk/google-vertex@3.0.25 and 3.0.127 (EmbeddingModelV2 providers). Root cause: EmbeddingModelV2 protocol does not include warnings in doEmbed return type.

signals.topic: Invalid tool call input stored as raw string causes API rejection on next step
signals.summary: When parseToolCall fails to parse JSON input, raw string is stored as input and passed to API on next step, causing rejection for providers like Amazon Bedrock that require input to be a JSON object
aliases: invalid tool call JSON input stored as raw string
tool call parse failure payload corruption
signals.review_reason: 明确用户影响：使用Amazon Bedrock provider时，模型解析错误的tool call后，下一步API直接拒绝请求，工具调用完全失败。虽非通用阻断（仅影响Bedrock用户），但对受影响用户是主流程失败，且破坏了模型看到tool-error并重试的能力。提供了明确复现步骤。

source_issues.title: Invalid tool call input stored as raw string causes API rejection on next step
source_issues.evidence: When model generates malformed JSON input for tool call, SDK stores raw string as input and marks tool invalid. On next API step, Amazon Bedrock API rejects with 'The format of the value at messages.X.content.Y.toolUse.input is invalid. Provide a json object'. The model never sees the tool-error result, breaking retry/fallback mechanism.

signals.topic: gateway.getAvailableModels() throws on new modelType 'reranking' — enum missing value
signals.summary: gateway.getAvailableModels() crashes because the SDK's hardcoded Zod enum only allows embedding/image/language/video but gateway now serves cohere/rerank-v3.5 with modelType 'reranking'
aliases: gateway metadata schema missing reranking modelType
getAvailableModels Zod validation failure new modelType
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：gateway.getAvailableModels()是用户发现和使用模型的核心API调用，一旦gateway上线新modelType就崩溃。由于enum硬编码，每次gateway增加新modelType都需要SDK发版修复，具有反复性。已确认今天(2026-04-14)线上触发。

source_issues.title: gateway.getAvailableModels() throws on cohere/rerank-v3.5: schema enum missing 'reranking'
source_issues.evidence: gateway.getAvailableModels() throws 'GatewayResponseError: Invalid error response format' because validation on success body fails on the 'reranking' enum value, then SDK re-validates against error schema, surfacing a misleading error. Root cause: Zod enum in gateway-fetch-metadata.ts only has 'embedding|image|language|video', missing 'reranking'. This is the same class of bug as #12732 (video modelType was the previous trigger).

signals.topic: MCP HTTP transport does not downgrade mcp-protocol-version header after negotiation — breaks Figma Dev Mode MCP
signals.summary: HttpMCPTransport always sends LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION in headers after initialize, ignoring negotiated protocolVersion, causing 400 errors against servers like Figma Dev Mode MCP that support older versions
aliases: MCP protocol version header not negotiated
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：@ai-sdk/mcp连接Figma Dev Mode MCP Server时完全失败，客户端创建后永远无法完成初始化。是MCP transport的核心互操作性问题，且同时影响stable(1.x)和beta(2.x)版本。已提供完整curl抓包复现。

source_issues.title: [@ai-sdk/mcp] Streamable HTTP transport does not downgrade mcp-protocol-version header after version negotiation (breaks servers like Figma Dev Mode MCP)
source_issues.evidence: After initialize returns protocolVersion '2025-06-18', the transport still sends '2025-11-25' in subsequent requests, triggering 400 'Unsupported protocol version' from Figma Dev Mode MCP Server. createMCPClient never resolves — the notifications/initialized request is rejected. Direct curl with correct version in header succeeds. Affects both @ai-sdk/mcp 1.x and 2.x beta.

signals.topic: Turbopack compiler fails to generate next/root-params exports when rootParams: true is enabled
signals.summary: When rootParams: true is set in next.config.js, the Turbopack compiler does not generate named param functions exported from next/root-params, breaking the root params feature entirely for Turbopack users.
signals.review_reason: Three independent reports confirm that enabling rootParams with Turbopack produces zero exports, completely breaking the feature for any user relying on it (e.g., next-intl integration). This is a main-flow feature failure.

source_issues.title: [Turbopack] next/root-params has no exports when rootParams: true is enabled
source_issues.evidence: Turbopack compiler fails to generate named param functions from next/root-params when rootParams: true is enabled, making the API unusable.

source_issues.title: [Turbopack] rootParams: next/root-params exports not generated by compiler
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as 92744 — Turbopack not generating root-params exports; reproduction repo confirmed.

source_issues.title: [Turbopack] rootParams: next/root-params has no exports - compiler does not generate named param functions
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as 92744 — compiler does not generate named param functions for next/root-params.

signals.topic: Malformed Origin header in Server Actions triggers unhandled TypeError causing HTTP 500 DoS
signals.summary: When a malformed Origin header is sent to a self-hosted Next.js application with Server Actions, new URL(originHeader) throws an unhandled TypeError in the CSRF check, returning HTTP 500 instead of 400, enabling denial of service.
signals.review_reason: Three reports confirm an unhandled TypeError in Server Actions CSRF check triggered by malformed Origin headers, causing HTTP 500 responses that can be exploited for denial of service on self-hosted Next.js deployments.

source_issues.title: Malformed Origin header in Next.js Server Actions returns HTTP 500 instead of 400
source_issues.evidence: A malformed Origin header causes new URL() to throw TypeError in the CSRF check, returning HTTP 500 instead of a proper 400; a public PoC repo demonstrates the DoS.

source_issues.title: SECURITY ALERT: new URL(originHeader) in Server Actions CSRF check throws unhandled TypeError on malformed Origin headers, causing DoS (HTTP 500)
source_issues.evidence: Security vulnerability confirmed with PoC repo: unhandled TypeError from malformed Origin causes server to return 500, enabling denial of service on self-hosted Pages Router deployments.

source_issues.title: SECURITY ALERT: new URL(originHeader) in Server Actions CSRF check throws unhandled TypeError on malformed Origin headers, causing DoS (HTTP 500)
source_issues.evidence: Points to source code location in action-handler.ts where unhandled TypeError occurs on malformed Origin; same DoS mechanism as 92703.

signals.topic: next/dynamic preload links missing crossOrigin attribute causes CORS failures on cross-origin asset serving
signals.summary: When assets are served from a different domain with crossOrigin: 'anonymous' configured in next.config.js, dynamically imported chunk preloads do not include the crossorigin attribute, causing CORS warnings or blocking prefetch.
aliases: crossOrigin missing on dynamic import preloads
signals.review_reason: Users serving assets on a different domain with crossOrigin configured experience CORS failures on prefetched dynamic chunks, breaking lazy-loaded component loading in cross-origin setups.

source_issues.title: next/dynamic preloads missing crossOrigin setting
source_issues.evidence: Preload links injected for next/dynamic imports do not carry the crossorigin attribute even when crossOrigin is set in next.config.js, leading to CORS errors when assets are served from a different domain.

signals.topic: Object.fromEntries(URLSearchParams) drops duplicate query parameter keys causing stale UI on navigation
signals.summary: When navigating with duplicate query parameters (e.g. ?color=red&color=blue), using Object.fromEntries on URLSearchParams loses the duplicates, resulting in incorrect UI state.
signals.review_reason: Navigation with duplicate query parameters silently produces incorrect UI state — the URL reflects the correct parameters but the rendered content shows stale data, directly breaking user-facing form and filter interactions.

source_issues.title: Object.fromEntries(URLSearchParams) drops duplicate keys → stale UI on navigation
source_issues.evidence: Adding a second value to a multi-select query param (e.g., ?color=red + ?color=blue) results in 4 items instead of 2, demonstrating that duplicate keys are dropped and stale state is shown.

signals.topic: Memory leak in Next.js SSR when running with Bun runtime (bun next start)
signals.summary: A memory leak is observed in Next.js server-side rendering when using the Bun JavaScript runtime with 'bun next start', causing gradual memory growth and eventual server instability.
signals.review_reason: Memory leak in SSR causes gradual resource exhaustion and eventual server crashes in Bun deployments; while Bun is a third-party runtime, it is officially supported and users experience real production instability.

source_issues.title: Memory leak in Next.js SSR under bun --bun next start
source_issues.evidence: A standalone reproduction repo demonstrates memory growth in SSR when running Next.js with Bun runtime, leading to resource exhaustion over time.

signals.topic: SIGKILL/SIGINT sent to turbo not forwarded to child tasks, causing orphaned processes and broken integration with Playwright/testing tools
signals.summary: When turbo receives SIGKILL or SIGINT, child processes (e.g., `pnpm run dev` servers) continue running. This is incompatible with Playwright testing which sends SIGKILL on test closure, leaving dev servers hanging. The issue affects both SIGINT (graceful shutdown) and SIGKILL (force kill).
aliases: signal not forwarded to child processes
turbo kill does not stop child tasks
signals.review_reason: Two separate signal issues (SIGINT #9694, SIGKILL #9666) with 31 combined comments and active engagement. Both result in orphaned child processes. SIGKILL issue directly breaks the Playwright + turbo integration, a very common testing setup. This is a main flow failure for local development and testing workflows.

source_issues.title: `SIGINT` being sent to `turbo` is not forwarded to underlying tasks
source_issues.evidence: kill -SIGINT ${TURBO_PID} does not result in SIGINT being sent to child tasks. 22 comments, actively being worked.

source_issues.title: On SIGKILL to `turbo run`, tasks continue running (incompatible with Playwright testing)
source_issues.evidence: kill -9 on turbo run leaves dev servers running. Playwright sends SIGKILL on test closure, so turbo + Playwright combinations result in hanging processes. Confirmed not reproducible with direct `next dev` or `pnpm run dev`. Affects all monorepo users using turbo with testing tools.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker creates incomplete output for pnpm, breaking CI/CD Docker builds
signals.summary: When running `turbo prune --docker` with pnpm, the pruned output only contains `package.json` files but no stub files for `bin` entries. This causes pnpm to refuse creating `.bin` shim entries, making the `copy json -> pnpm install -> copy full -> turbo build` Docker workflow fail when build scripts depend on binary tools.
aliases: turbo prune missing bin stubs for pnpm
signals.review_reason: CI/CD Docker prune workflow is broken for pnpm users when dependent packages produce binary tools. This is a main flow failure in a documented use case (the official Docker guide), causing builds to fail silently.

source_issues.title: prune --docker: create stub source files for bin entries
source_issues.evidence: pnpm refuses to create .bin entries when only package.json is present; the copy json -> pnpm install -> copy full -> turbo build sequence fails if any build script needs a binary tool that relies on a .bin shim. User provides a full reproduction repo.

signals.topic: turbo run --filter with source control changes does not detect changes, breaking affected-based builds in CI
signals.summary: Using `--filter="[origin/main..HEAD]"` with `turbo run` does not pick up the same changes that `git show origin/main..HEAD` detects. Affected-based builds silently skip changed packages, causing stale builds in CI pipelines.
aliases: source control filter not detecting changes
turbo filter git changes not detected
signals.review_reason: Core CI/CD workflow is broken. Affected-based builds are a primary use case for turbo in CI, and the git-source-control filter silently returns no tasks despite git confirming changes exist. This is a main flow failure that directly wastes CI time and produces stale artifacts.

source_issues.title: Filtering by source control changes doesn't detect changes
source_issues.evidence: git show origin/main..HEAD outputs commit info, but turbo run --filter="[origin/main..HEAD]" outputs no directories. Using --affected instead does detect changes correctly. This breaks CI/CD affected-based build strategies.

signals.topic: Turbo > 2.8.14 fails to connect to self-hosted remote cache with custom CA, cache effectively broken for enterprise users
signals.summary: After upgrading past 2.8.14, turbo frequently fails to connect to self-hosted remote cache servers that use custom Certificate Authorities. The error is intermittent and non-deterministic. This effectively breaks remote caching for enterprise/self-hosted setups.
aliases: custom CA remote cache connection failure
turbo remote cache CA certificate error
signals.review_reason: Remote caching is a core turbo value proposition, and a regression after 2.8.14 breaks it for all self-hosted cache users with custom CAs. Every build becomes a full rebuild (cache miss), causing significant CI time waste and cost increase across all affected enterprise teams.

source_issues.title: Turbo > 2.8.14 fails to connect to self-hosted remote cache server with custom CA
source_issues.evidence: All turbo versions > 2.8.14 produce 'Could not connect to remote cache' warnings with self-hosted caches using custom CAs. Every build results in cache misses despite previously working. Users bisect the issue to ApiClient refactoring that introduced the fast client. Multiple platforms affected (macOS ARM64, multiple Linux distros amd64).

signals.topic: Tasks silently skipped with no explanation during turbo runs, cache invalidation unpredictably fails
signals.summary: Running `turbo tsc` sometimes executes only 1 out of 15 expected tasks, with no error messages or explanation. The issue is non-deterministic and relates to daemon/package discovery timeouts. Affected tasks report wrong package names and incorrect scope. Users cannot trust turbo's cache correctness.
signals.review_reason: Tasks silently executing partially with no error is a critical reliability issue. Users cannot trust turbo's correctness, and partial builds can produce stale artifacts that are hard to debug. The non-deterministic nature makes it especially dangerous in CI where builds may appear to pass while actually skipping critical tasks.

source_issues.title: Tasks getting skipped with no explanation
source_issues.evidence: Running turbo tsc repeatedly from a subdirectory produces 15 cached tasks (correct) in some runs and only 1 task (incorrect) in others. Debug logs show wrong package scope and a tsc task being scheduled for a package that has no tsc task. Related to daemon package discovery timeout falling back to local strategy.

signals.topic: vercel domains add invalidates production aliases causing DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND cascade to all subdomains via locked wildcard ALIAS record
signals.summary: Running `vercel domains add` on a subdomain invalidates the root domain's production alias, and the auto-managed locked wildcard ALIAS record (`* ALIAS cname.vercel-dns-XXX.com`) propagates DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND to every subdomain across 21 projects simultaneously, with ~19 hours of downtime and no user-mitigation path.
aliases: wildcard ALIAS propagates DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND to all subdomains
signals.review_reason: This is a P0-class incident: adding a subdomain via CLI invalidates the root domain's production alias, and the platform-managed locked wildcard ALIAS record (which users cannot delete or edit) cascades DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND to every subdomain across ALL projects on the account. User impact is severe: 21 projects down, 19 hours downtime, no user-facing mitigation path. The lock on the wildcard record means users cannot self-resolve. This blocks the primary deployment workflow and causes multi-project outage.

source_issues.title: vercel domains add invalidates production aliases, causing DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND cascade via uneditable wildcard ALIAS records
source_issues.evidence: 21 Vercel projects went down simultaneously, 12 actively deployed services unreachable, link shortener used in 886+ published articles unreachable, ~19 hours total downtime, recovery required manual Vercel API calls to re-alias root domain. Wildcard ALIAS record is locked and cannot be deleted or edited by users to mitigate.

signals.topic: Next.js 16 post-build validation drops intermediate path segments for multi-segment Root Directory, causing ENOENT build failures
signals.summary: Post-build validation for Next.js 16 deployments uses only the basename of the Root Directory instead of the full path, causing ENOENT errors on valid files that exist on disk, and blocking deployments for monorepo users with multi-segment Root Directory settings.
aliases: monorepo Root Directory path validation error
Next.js 16 post-build ENOENT on valid files
signals.review_reason: This blocks the deployment workflow for monorepo users with multi-segment Root Directory settings (e.g., clients/admin-ui). The build itself completes successfully but post-build validation fails with ENOENT on files that exist on disk — meaning the deployment never goes live. The required workaround (symlink hack during build) is non-obvious and places an undue burden on users. This is a clear regression introduced in Next.js 16.2.3.

source_issues.title: Next.js 16 post-build validation drops intermediate path segments from multi-segment Root Directory
source_issues.evidence: Build fails at post-build validation step (after 'Build Completed' message) for any monorepo with a multi-segment Root Directory (e.g., clients/admin-ui). Files exist at correct path on disk but validator looks at wrong path (dropping 'clients/' segment). Workaround requires symlinking during build. Blocks deployment for affected monorepo setups.

signals.topic: vercel env add preview ignores --yes --force flags and prompts for git branch, blocking CI/CD pipelines
signals.summary: Running `vercel env add <name> preview --yes --force` still interactively prompts for a git branch, causing CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, etc.) to hang indefinitely since they cannot respond to the prompt.
aliases: vercel env add preview --yes flag ignored
preview env var CLI prompt blocks CI
vercel env add interactive prompt in non-interactive mode
signals.review_reason: This blocks the environment variable configuration workflow in CI/CD pipelines. The CLI's own hint message suggests a command that does not work, making this especially confusing. Users must fall back to raw REST API calls to add preview environment variables in automation — the documented CLI flags are completely non-functional. Affects GitHub Actions and other CI systems.

source_issues.title: CLI: vercel env add <name> preview always prompts for git branch even with --yes --force
source_issues.evidence: The CLI suggests an exact command in its error hint output, but running that exact command still triggers the interactive prompt. Pipeline hangs indefinitely. Workaround requires direct REST API calls, bypassing the CLI entirely. Affects all CI/CD environments.

signals.topic: User account login blocked with no explanation or recovery path — 'user_blocked' error with no actionable information
signals.summary: Users are blocked from logging into Vercel via GitHub OAuth with a generic 'user_blocked' error, with no explanation of why the account was blocked, no way to determine the cause, and no clear recovery path to regain access.
aliases: Vercel login blocked no recovery path
signals.review_reason: Complete account lockout with no user-understandable explanation or recovery path is a critical auth failure. Users cannot access their projects, deployments, or any Vercel services. The opaque 'user_blocked' error with no reason and no support response creates a situation where users have zero agency to resolve the issue themselves.

source_issues.title: Unable to login any longer and I don't know why...
source_issues.evidence: User is completely locked out of their Vercel account. Error message is 'user_blocked' with no reason or remediation steps. Attempted to contact via email but received no useful response. No clarity on why the block occurred or how to resolve it. Account access is entirely denied.

signals.topic: Rust runtime v2 fails with 'address already in use' during vercel dev function invocation
signals.summary: Using Vercel's Rust beta runtime with `vercel dev` results in 'address already in use' errors on function invocation, causing the Rust function to exit before completing the request.
aliases: Rust v2 runtime address in use error
vercel dev Rust beta runtime crash
Rust runtime lambda error address in use
signals.review_reason: Rust runtime v2 is beta but users actively trying it hit a consistent crash (EADDRINUSE) on every function invocation, making the Rust development workflow completely non-functional. While marked beta, this is a clear runtime failure that defeats the purpose of the feature for any user attempting to use it.

source_issues.title: Rust runtime v2 fails with 'address already in use'
source_issues.evidence: Rust beta runtime crashes with EADDRINUSE on function invocation in `vercel dev`. Function exits before completing request. Affects local development with Rust v2 runtime. Reproducible by multiple users (related to issue #14532).

signals.topic: File system watchers fail to detect external file changes and new files
signals.summary: Zed's file system watchers do not detect changes made outside the editor, causing the Project Panel and file explorer to show stale content, files not to appear after creation, and ghost edited markers on unchanged files.
aliases: files highlighted as edited without changes
signals.review_reason: File system watching is a core development workflow requirement. Three independent reports confirm that Zed fails to detect external file changes across local and remote projects. Users lose visibility into their file tree, see ghost edit markers, and cannot track project state—directly degrading the editing experience.

source_issues.title: Project Panel content won't be updateded
source_issues.evidence: Project Panel shows empty or stale content even when folder has files. Files and folders created externally (via terminal, Finder, or copy operations inside Zed) do not appear. File watcher appears broken for certain folders.

source_issues.title: Zed is getting worse
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports: 'Zed does not pick up changes in files. It highlights files as edited even though they are not. It keeps showing files that no longer exist.' Demonstrates persistent file state tracking failure.

source_issues.title: New remote files do not show up in file explorer
source_issues.evidence: Files created on remote server via integrated terminal do not appear in Zed's file explorer even after several minutes. Remote file watcher not functioning.

signals.topic: Windows sandbox blocks AI agent shell command execution
signals.summary: On Windows, Zed's sandboxed shell commands fail immediately with 'windows sandbox: spawn setup refresh' error when Default permissions are selected, making AI agent tool execution completely non-functional on Windows regardless of workspace.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker: AI agent tool execution (shell commands) is completely broken on Windows when using Default permissions—the intended and recommended security setting. The error occurs on trivial commands and is not workspace-specific, indicating a systemic Windows sandbox initialization failure.

source_issues.title: Sandboxed shell commands fail immediately with Default permssions
source_issues.evidence: Sandboxed shell commands fail immediately with 'windows sandbox: spawn setup refresh'. Failure happens even for trivial commands (Get-Location, Get-ChildItem) and across unrelated workspaces. Default permissions mode is broken; only 'Full' mode works. Error logged: 'exec error: windows sandbox: spawn setup refresh'.

signals.topic: Gemini API requests fail with Invalid JSON payload error across all Gemini models
signals.summary: All Gemini API requests fail with HTTP 400 Invalid JSON payload error due to malformed tool parameter schema in Zed's request construction, blocking AI chat functionality for all Gemini users.
signals.review_reason: AI chat via Gemini is completely non-functional for all Gemini users due to malformed JSON payload in API requests. Error originates from Zed's tool parameter schema construction, not from user misconfiguration or API-side issues. Clear user-blocking evidence in error log.

source_issues.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro request error
source_issues.evidence: API error on ANY Gemini request (even Gemini Flash). Error: 'Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "type" at tools[0].function_declarations[6].parameters.properties[4].value.properties[4].value: Proto field is not repeating, cannot start list.' This is a schema mismatch in Zed's tool definition construction, not a user configuration issue.

signals.topic: Vim mode search with n/N selects all text between matches instead of jumping
signals.summary: Regression: pressing n or N in Vim mode selects all text between the previous and current search match rather than just moving the cursor, breaking the core Vim search navigation pattern.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed regression that breaks a core Vim editing workflow. The n/N navigation pattern is fundamental to Vim usage, and the incorrect behavior makes the editor unusable for Vim-mode users on what should be routine operations.

source_issues.title: vim mode: search by pressing `n` selects everything between matches instead of jumping to next match
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression. When pressing n or N after * or # search, Zed selects both the current and previous match highlight plus all text between them, instead of moving the cursor. The * / # keys behave correctly, but n/N do not. Explicitly noted as a recent regression.

signals.topic: Loose file session state not restored on startup on Windows
signals.summary: On Windows, Zed with 'restore_on_startup: last_session' fails to restore loose files on restart due to 'Invalid window handle' errors during session serialization, losing user's open work context.
signals.review_reason: Users lose their open work context entirely on Windows restart despite explicitly configuring session restoration. The 'Invalid window handle' error during session serialization is a clear data loss path—not a one-off startup glitch but a systemic session save failure.

source_issues.title: Session with loose files not restored on startup on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Despite 'restore_on_startup: last_session' and 'on_last_window_closed: quit_app' settings, Zed opens blank on Windows restart—no files restored. Logs show 'window not found' and 'Invalid window handle' errors during serialization: 'Error { code: HRESULT(0x80040102), message: "Invalid window handle" }'
